units.la: Ὅτι τὸ αὐτὸ ἢ δικαιοσύνη μου πρὸς ἐαυτὸν ἢ ὅσ; ἐὰν μὴ ἐχρῆσθαι, χαίρομαι αὐτῇ, πρὸς τὸ ἔργον, ὡς ὀργάνῳ, παρὰ τὴν τῆς ὅλον φύσεως δοθὲν τι. Ἐὰν μὴ ἐχαρῆ, ἥδη προσχωρῶ τὸ ἔργον τῷ δυναμένῳ κρεῖττον ἀποτελεῖσθαι, ἐὰν ἄλλως ἔχω μὴ καθήκην, ἢ πρόσ-
units.tr: My own justice and goodness, toward myself and others, are these: if I am not hindered, I rejoice in them as a tool is rejoiced in for the work it does, as given by the nature of the whole. If I am not rejoicing, I turn at once to the work that can be done better by one who is able, if I am otherwise and unsuited to it, or

units.la: ὡς δύναμαι, προσπαλαίων τὸ δυσκόλον[?], καὶ πρόσχρησιν τῷ ἐμῷ ἡγεμονικῷ, ποιῆσαι τὸ εἰς τὴν κοινωνίαν ἀνῶ[?] καίειον, καὶ χρήσιμον. ὅπῃ δ' ἂν ἐμαυτῷ, ἢ σοὶ ἄλλῳ ποιῶ, ὧδε μόνον χρὴ ζῶν τὸν ἐνδοτῆν, ἐς τὸ κοινὸν χρήσιμον, ὃ δύαρμοσθαι[?]. Ὅσοι μὲν τὸ ὄλον ὑμνοῦντες ἢ ἡ λήθη παραδίδοντα[?]· ὅσοι δὲ τύτες ὑμνοῦντες, παλαι ἐκ τοῦ[?] ποιῶν; Μὴ ἀλλως βοηθεῖσθαι[?]. πρόχρῃ γὰρ οἱ ἀνθρώπων ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἐμαυτῷ[?], ὡς γραπώτην αἱ τεχνῶν[?] μαχία. Τί οὖν, ἐὰν σὺ μὴ χρηλαίνων ἐν τῷ ἐπαλλαξιν[?] ἀναβλῶσαι μόνος μὴ ἀλλὰ ἀλλον, σὺ δὲ ἀλλου[?] ἡ τὸ; Τὰ μέλλοντα μὴ παρασάτω. ἡξὲς γὰρ ἐπ' αὐτὰ, ἐὰν δύνῃ, φέρων τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον, ᾧ νῦν πρὸς τὰ πρόντα χρῆ. Πάντα ἀμμίλοις ἀδιατλέκεται[?]; ἡ συγκράτησις ἱερά, καὶ ξεδὸν τι ἡδὺν ἀλλότριον ἄλλο ἄλλῳ. Συγκατάτακ ἔτι ἡ συγκοσμεῖν αὐτὸν κόσμον. Κόσμος τε γὰρ εἷς ἁπάντων, ἡ θεὸς εἷς ἁπάντων, καὶ οὐσία μία, καὶ νόμος εἷς. Λόγος κοινὸς πάντων τῶν νοερῶν ζῴων, καὶ ἀλήθεια μία, εἴγε ἡ τελειότης μία τῶν ὁμογενῶν, ἡ τῶν αὐτῶν λόγου μετεχόντων ζῴων. Πάντων ἡ ὕλη, ὡς ἀφανίζει τὰ ἴσα τῇ τοῦ ὅλου οὐσία· ἡ πάντων αὐτὸν, ὡς τὸ τοῦ ὅλου λόγου τὰ ἴσα ἀναλαμβάνει· ἡ πάντως μηνὸς μὴ τὰ ἴσα ἐγκαταχώννυται τῷ αἰῶνι. Τῷ λογικῷ ζῴῳ ἡ αὐτὴ πρᾶξις καὶ φύσιν ὀξεῖα, καὶ λόγον ὀρθόν[?] μέλεος. οἷον ὅσιν, οἷς ἡνωμένοις, τὰ μέλη τοῦ σώμα- τος, τὸν ἔχει τὸν λόγον, οἱ διεξῶσι, τὰ λογικά, πρὸς μίαν τινὰ ἐνέργειαν καταπεπλυασμένα[?].
units.tr: as far as I can, wrestling with what is difficult and making my governing mind useful to the community, so that what I do for myself or for another is fitting and useful to the common good. Whatever I do to myself or to another, I must live with this only in mind, that it be fitting to the common good. Some people, praising the whole, or ... those who forget ... Do not be helped otherwise. For people are of use to one another in their own ways, as the hand and the foot... Then what, if you, not steering in the exchange, ... wish to rise alone, but not another, or you of another?... Let future things not disturb you. For you will come to them, if you can, carrying the same reason with which you now deal with present things. All things are bound together by a holy kinship, and each thing is nearly akin to every other. For there is one world ordered out of all things, one God through all things, one substance and one law, one common reason of all intelligent creatures, and one truth, since there is one perfection for creatures of the same kind that share in the same reason. All matter is absorbed into the substance of the whole, as all the things of the whole are taken up into its reason, and all are quickly covered over by time. For a rational creature there is one and the same course: to act with a sharp nature and to keep a right reason. As the members of a body, joined together, have one function, so rational beings, separated, are yet shaped for one common activity.

units.la: μᾶλλον δέ σοι ἡ τότε νόησις προσποιήσεται, ἐὰν πρὸς ἑαυτὸν πολλάκις λέγῃς, ὅτι μέλος εἰμὶ τῷ ἐν τῷ λογικῷ συστήματος. ἐὰν δὲ ἀλλὰ τῷ ῥᾳδίως μέρος ἐστὶν ἑαυτῷ λέγῃς, ὅπως ἀρα ἀπὸ φιλίας ἑαυτοῦ ἀνθρώπους· ὅπως καταλαμβάνῃ ... [illegible, ~12 letters] ... ἐπὶ ὡς πέτον αὐτὸ φιλὸν ποιῆς· ὅπως ὡς αὐτὸ οὐ ποιῶν.
units.tr: Rather, the thought of this will come to you more readily if you often say to yourself that you are a member of the rational system. But if you say to yourself, more lightly, that you are a part, you do not yet love people from the heart; beneficence does not yet give you pleasure, but you do it as a mere duty, not as it should be done ... (illegible).

units.la: Ὁ δὲ ἐξωσθὲν πρὸ ἐξ πέτῳ ζῆς παθεῖν ἐν τῇ προαιρετικῇ[?] ... [illegible, ~10 letters] ... πέτως ταύτης δυναμένοις. ἐκεῖνα δ' ἐὰν ἡ ἑλκῆ, μέμψῃ τὰ παθήματα. ἐγὼ δ' ἐὰν μὴ ἀπολάβω, ὅτι κακὸν τὸ συμβεβηκὸς, ὅπως βελλάμμαι. ἔξεστί μοι μὴ ἀπολαβεῖν. Ὃ, πᾶν τις ποιῇ ἢ λέγῃ, ἐμὲ δεῖ ἀγαθὸν εἶναι. ὡς ἂν εἰ ὁ χρυσὸς ἢ ὁ σμάραγδος, ἢ ἡ πορφύρα, ἐξ ἐπὶ ἑλεγεν, ὅ, τις ἂν ποιῇ, ἢ λέγῃ, ἐμὲ δὲ σμάραγδον εἶναι, μὴ τὸ ἐμαυτῆς χρῶμα ἔχειν. Τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν, αὐτὸ ἑαυτῷ, οὐχ ἑνοχλεῖ. οὐδὲ λέγω, ὃ φοβεῖ ἑαυτὸ εἰς ἰδίαν μίαν. εἰ δὲ τὶς ἄλλῳ αὐτὸ φοβήσοι, ἢ λυπῆσαι, δεῖ ἀ, ποιέ- τω. αὐτὸ γὰρ ἑαυτὸ ἐνολυπτικῶς τὸ πρᾶγμα εἰς τοιαύτας τροπάς. Τὸ σῶμα μὴ πάθῃ τι, αὐτὸ μεμνηνται ἀ ἑ διώατα, ἡ λεγέτω, εἴ τι πάσχει. Τὸ δὲ ψυχαλεῖον, τὸ φοβούμενον, τὸ λυπούμενον, τὸ ἐκεῖ τὴν ὅλης ἐνλαμβανόμενον, ὅ δὲν μὴ πά-
units.tr: The one who has been pushed out... (illegible) ... you must suffer in the power of choice ... (illegible). If you blame those things, you blame the sufferings. But if I do not accept that what has happened is evil, I am not harmed. I am free not to accept it. Whatever anyone does or says, I must be good, just as gold, or an emerald, or purple, says always: whatever anyone does or says, I must remain emerald and keep my own colour. The governing mind is not disturbed by itself; I do not say that it frightens itself into a particular fear. If anyone else frightens or grieves it, let him do so; for the mind itself does not turn such things into those changes. The body, if it suffers anything, may say what it suffers. But the little soul, which fears and grieves, and which takes the judgement of the things about it, let it not suffer.

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters] ἡ. ὅτι ἐξῆς αὐτοῖς κεῖσθαι διαυτῷ. ἀπροσδεὲς ὅσον ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ, τὸ ἡγεμονικόν, ἐὰν μὴ ἑαυτῷ ἐνδόξα ποιῇ· κατὰ ταῦτα ὁ αὐτάρκης, καὶ ἀνεμπόδιστον, ἐὰν μὴ ἑαυτὸ ταραχῇ, καὶ ἐμπο-δίζῃ. Εὐδαιμονία ἐστὶ, δαίμων ἀγαθός, ἢ ἀγαθόν. τί δὲ ὧδε ποιεῖς, ὦ φαντασία; ἀπέρχῃ σὺ ὡς ἦλθες, ὅτι χρήζω σου. ἐλήλυθας ὃ κ' τὸ ἀρχαῖον ἔθος. οὐ γὰρ ὀργίζομαί σοι. μόνον ἀπῄθι. Φοβεῖ ταί τις μεταβολῆ. τί δ' ἐὰν ὕδωρ ... εἰς μεταβολῆς; οὐχ ὁρᾷς ὅτι ἢ αὐτὸ τὸ σε μεταβάλλειν ὅμοιόν ἐστι, ἢ ὁμοίως ἀναγκαῖον τῇ τῇ ὅλῳ φύσει· διεκπορεύει τὰ σώματα, τῷ ὅλῳ συμφυῇ σωτηρίᾳ, ὡς τὰ ἡμέτερα μέρη ἀλλήλοις.
units.tr: ... (illegible) ... that they lie outside it. The governing mind, so far as it is itself concerned, needs nothing, unless it makes its own needs by its opinions. Accordingly the self-sufficient and unhindered mind is not disturbed, unless it disturbs and hinders itself. Happiness is a good spirit, or a good state. But why do you do this, O fancy? Go away as you came, for I have no need of you. You came according to your old custom; I am not angry with you; only go away. Do you fear change? But what would exist without change? Do you not see that your own changing is like the nature of the whole, and as necessary? Bodies pass through; the whole is kept whole by its own changing, just as our parts change into one another.

units.la: πόσος ἤδη ὁ αἰὼν Χρυσίππος, πόσος Σωκράτης, πόσος Ἐπίκτητος καὶ ἄπειρος [?].
units.tr: How long already is the age of Chrysippus, how long of Socrates, how long of Epictetus, and of countless others.

units.la: ἀλλ' αὐτὸς ἵνα ἑαυτὸν ὑπνοσοῦ σοι ἀνθρώπων τε καὶ πραγμάτων, πρὸς αὐτὸ πέτ[?]ω.
units.tr: But do not hold yourself to people and affairs as though you were loosed from them; turn to yourself.

units.la: ἐμὲ οὖν μόνον πειρᾶσθαι, μὴ πρὸς αὐτὸς ποιῶ, ὃ ἂν καταδοκῶ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἄλλο, ἢ ὡς ἂν θέλει, ἢ ὅπως ἂν θέλῃ. ἐγγὺς μὲν ἡ ἡ τοῦ αὐτὴν λήθη. ἐγγὺς δὲ ἦσαν— ἡ πρὸς τὸν λόγον[?].
units.tr: Therefore let me only try not to do anything to others as I would not wish, or as someone would not wish done to him. Forgetting the one who is near at hand ... and near at hand ... to reason.

units.la: Ἴδιον ἀνθρώπου φιλεῖν καὶ τοὺς ἡμαρτηκότας[?]. Τοῦτο δὲ γίνεται, ἐὰν συμπροσπίπτῃ σοι, ὅπου καὶ συγγενεῖς, καὶ δι᾽ ἀγνοιαν, ἢ ἀκοντὸς ἁμαρτάνουσι[?]· ὡς μετ᾽ ὀλίγον ἀμφότεροι τεθνήξεσθε. Καὶ πρὸς τῶν αὐτῶν, ὅ[?] ἂν ἐλαττώσῃ. Ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν οὐ χείρον ἐποίησεν, ἢ πρόσθεσιν[?]. Ἡ τὴν ὅλην φύσιν, ἐν τῇ ὅλης οὐσίας, ὡς ἡμεῖς, νῦν μὲν ἴππαιον ἐδλασε[?]· συγχέασα δὲ ζῷον, εἰς δανίδου φύσιν, συνεχῆ σαυτῇ τῇ ὕλῃ αὐτῆς. Εἶτα εἰς ἀνθρωπάρεον, εἶτα εἰς ἄλλο τι.
units.tr: It is proper to a human being to love even those who have done wrong. This happens if you consider that they are kinsmen, and that they err through ignorance or against their will; and soon you will both be dead. And, above all, there is what the mind has made worse, or rather added. Nature, which is the whole substance, out of which we are made, now makes a horse, now mingles other living things into the nature of a tree, and continues to its own matter. Then it makes a human being, then something else.

units.la: Ἕκαστον δὲ τούτων, πρὸς ὀλίγιστον ὑπέσχε[?]. Δεινὸν δὲ οὐδέν, τὸ ἐξαλυθῶναι τῷ κόσμῳ· ὥσπερ καὶ συμπαγῆναι. Τὸ ἐπίκτητον τῆς προσώπου λίαν πρὸς φύσιν, ὅταν πολλάκις ἀποθνήσκῃ ἢ προάγμα[?]. Ἢ τὸ τελευταῖον ἀποξβέσθη, ὥστε ὅλως ἐξ ἀφθαλμῶν μὴ ἴδωσι[?]. Αὐτῷ γε τούτῳ προακολουθεῖν πειρῶ, ὅπου πρὸς λόγον. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ ἡ σωματίωσις τῆς ἁμαρτάνῃ, οἰχήσεται, τίς ἐπὶ τῷ ζῷ αἰτία; Πάντα ὅσα ὁρᾷς, ὅσον οὔπω, μεταβαλεῖ ἢ τὰ ὅλα διοικοῦσα φύσις, καὶ ἄλλα ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας αὐτῶν ποιήσει. Καὶ πάλιν ἄλλα ἐκ τῆς ἐκείνων οὐσίας, ἵνα ἀεὶ νέος ᾖ ὁ κόσμος.
units.tr: Each of these lasts only a very short time. Nor is it terrible to be dissolved into the world, as it is terrible to be put together. The change in a person's form, when it so often dies or ... the last ... is extinguished, so that they wholly disappear from sight. Try to follow this very thing, as far as reason goes. For if even the body is changed, where does the fault lie in this? All the things you see will soon be changed, and nature that governs the whole will make other things out of their substance, and again other things out of theirs, so that the world may always be new.

units.la: Ὅταν τις ἁμάρτῃ πρὸς σέ, σὺ δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἢ κακὸν συμπαλαίειν ἡμάρτε. Ὅρα γὰρ ἰδιὸν ἐλεῆσαι αὐτὸν, ἢ οὔτε θαυμάσεις, οὔτε ὀργισθῆναι. ἤτοι γὰρ καὶ αὐτὸς τὸ αὐτὸ ἐκείνῳ ἀγαθὸν ἐπὶ ὑπολαμβάνεις, ἢ ἄλλο ὁμοειδὲς. Δεῖ οὖν συγγινώσκειν. εἰ δὲ μηκέτι ὑπολαμβάνεις τὰ τοιαῦτα ἀγαθὰ καὶ κακά, ξάον ὑμῖν ἔστω τῷ προφορᾷ. Μὴ τὰ ἀπόντα ὑπονοεῖν, ὡς ἤδη ὄντα, ἀλλὰ τὴν πρόνοιαν τὰ δεξιώτατα ἐκλογίζεσθαι, καὶ τούτων χάριν ὑπομιμνήσκεσθαι, πῶς ἂν ἐπιζητεῖτο, εἰ μὴ πρὸν· ἅμα μὲν τοι φυλάσσῃ, μὴ δὲ τὰ ἔτως ἀσμενίζειν αὐτοῖς, ἐθίσης ἐκπιμᾶν αὐτὰ, ὥστε ἐάν ποτε μὴ πρὴ, παραχθήσεταί. εἰς ἀνθ' σωφροσύνῃ. Φύσιν ἔχει τὸ λογικὸν ἡγεμονικὸν, ἑαυτῷ ἀρκεῖσθαι δικαιοπραγοῦντι, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸ τὸ ὄντος γαληνὸν ἔχοντι. Ἠξιλάφου τῷ φανταισίαν. ἡσύχον τῷ νοῦ ὑρροσασίαν. [illegible, ~12 letters]· τὸ αὐτὸς τὸ χρόνῳ, γνώει ὃν τὸ συμβαῖνον, ἢ ὅι, ἢ ἄλλῳ, δίελε καὶ μέρισον δ' ἐπεκέμενον, εἰς τὸ αἰτιῶδες καὶ ὑλικὸν. συνόησον τῷ ἐσχάτῳ ὥραν. Τὸ ἐκείνῳ ἁμαρτηθὲν, ἐκεῖ καταλίπε, ὅπερ ἡ ἁμαρτία ὑπόστησι. συμπεκτείνφ τῷ νόμ-σιν τοῖς λεγομένοις. εἰσδύεσθαι τὸν νοῦν εἰς τὰ γινόμενα ζῷ ποιοῦντα. Φαίσθρων σαυτὸν ἀζηλόττιτι καὶ αἰδοί, καὶ τῆ πρὸς δ' αὐτὰ μέσον ἀρετὴ καὶ κακίας ἀξιοφοεία. Φίλην δ' ἀνθρώπινον χρὴ ἀκολουθῆσαι ἀν ἡ κιν. Ἐκεῖνο μὲν φησιν, ὅτι πάντα νομίσῃ. Ἐπὶ δὲ δαίμονα τὰ στοιχεῖα, ἀρκεῖ ὑμεμνῆσθαι, ὅπερ τὰ πάντα νομίσῃ ἔχει, ἢ δηλίαν [?]
units.tr: When anyone sins against you, remember that he has made a mistake about what is good or evil. Look, you should pity him rather than marvel at him or grow angry. For either you yourself think the same thing good that he does, or something of the same kind, so you ought to forgive him. But if you no longer count such things as good and evil, you will bear the offence more easily. Do not imagine absent things as though they were already present, but reckon up the greatest advantages you have and remind yourself how eagerly they would be sought if they were not there. Take care, however, not to delight in them so much that you will be upset when they are gone. [illegible] Time [illegible]: consider what happens, whether to you, to another, or to someone else, and divide and separate it into its cause and its matter. Keep the end of life in view. Leave there the wrong that was done there, where the sin itself stands. Let your mind enter into the things that happen and do what is at hand. Make yourself modest, unenvious and shameless, and hold to virtue and vice in the middle, as the measure of worth. The rational part is by nature self-sufficient when it acts justly and keeps a calm relation to what is. [illegible] Death: whether it is a scattering into atoms, a mixing, a quenching, or a change of place.

units.la: ἀλλίαν ὀλίγα. Περὶ θανάτου, εἰ σκεδασμὸς ἄ-τομοι, ἢ κρᾶσις, ἢ σβέσις, ἢ μετάστασις. Περὶ τῶν ἀφόρητον, [?] χρονίζον, φοβεῖ-τον. Ἡ διάνοια τῆς ἑαυτοῦ ψυχῆς ἐκπεσεῖ, καὶ ὁ χειρότερον δὲ ἡγεμονικὸν γέγονεν. Τὰ ἐν καθ᾽ ἑαυτὰ μέρη τοῦ τοῦ τόνου, εἰς ἔξω ἀπὸ αὐτῶν ἀφεροῦνται. Περὶ δέξης, δὲ τὰς διανοίας αὐτῶν, οἷον; Οὐχ ἡ φεύγουσι· οὐχ ἡ διώκουσι. ἡ ὅπως αἱ ἕτεραι ἄλλαι ἐπ᾽ ἄλλαις ὑπὸ φοβοῦνται, κρύπτεσθαι τὰ πρότερα. Οὕτως οὖν τῷ βίῳ, τὰ πρότερα ὑπὸ τῆς ἐπαγωγῆς, τὰ χρόνου ἐκαλύφθη. Πλατωνικόν. Ὧν ἐν ὑπάρχει διάνοια μεγαλοπρεπής, θεωρία, παντὸς μὲν χρόνου, πέσης ἡ οὐσίας, ἔτι οἷά τούτῳ μέγα τι δοκεῖν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπου βίου; ἀδιώκτων, ἢ δ᾽ ὃς. Ἐκεῖνον δὲ θάνατον οὐ δεινόν τι ἡγήσεται ὁ τοιοῦτος; ἡ-σάγη. Ἀν πεθενικὸν, βασιλικὸς μὲν πεάτη, ἠακῶς δὲ ἀκούειν. αἰ ἀρχαὶ δὲ ὅσοι μὲν πεόσωπον ὑπήκοον ἔγ᾽ ἁμαρτίζεσθαι, ὅ καταλαμβάνει ὡς ἀελθὼ ἢ διάνοια, αὐτὸ δὲ ὑφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς μὴ ἁμαρτίζεσθαι, καὶ καταρρεῖσθαι,
units.tr: ...little. Concerning death: whether it is a scattering into atoms, or a blending, or an extinction, or a migration. Concerning pain, that it is unbearable, or lasting, or fearful. The mind of the soul falls away from itself, and the ruling part has become worse. The parts that are in themselves, and in the tone of the body, are carried off outward from them. Concerning fame, what are their minds, and what are they like? They do not avoid, they do not pursue; as other things are feared one after another, so the earlier things are hidden. So in life, the earlier things are covered over by the later, as time covers the past. Platonic. For whoever has a lofty mind, looking on all time and all being, will think human life no great thing. Such a man will not think death a dreadful thing. ... If a king has said it, it is royal to be spoken of, and it is fitting to hear it. Those who are in office, as far as they are concerned, are to be ruled by the mind, which is not to be ruled by itself or thrown into confusion.

units.la: Τοῖς πράγμασι τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἡμῶν χρεών.Μέλει γὰρ αὐτοῖς ἔδεν.
units.tr: We must use the good things of our life for the things themselves, for they care nothing for it.

units.la: Ἀθανάτοις τε θεοῖς, ὁ ἡμῖν χάρματα δοίης·Βίον ὁρίζειν, ὥστε καρπίμον σάχυν.
units.tr: [Ἀθανάτοις τε θεοῖς, ὁ ἡμῖν χάρματα δοίης· Βίον ὁρίζειν, ὥστε καρπίμον σάχυν.] May you grant us joys, you immortal gods, and set our life so that it bears ripe ears of grain.

units.la: Καὶ δὴ μὲν εἶναι, τὸ δὲ μή.
units.tr: [Καὶ δὴ μὲν εἶναι, τὸ δὲ μή.] So let this be, and let that not be.

units.la: Εἰ δ' ἡμελήθη ἐν Θεῷ, καὶ παῖδ' ἐμῷ, Ἐχθ[?] λόγον καὶ ἔσορ.
units.tr: [Εἰ δ' ἡμελήθη ἐν Θεῷ, καὶ παῖδ' ἐμῷ...] But if it was neglected by God, and by my child, ... word and look.

units.la: Τὸ γὰρ δ' ὧν μετ' ἐμὲ καὶ ἂ δίκαιον, μὴ ξυνεπι[?] ἀρλωεῖν, μὴ σφύζειν.
units.tr: For what comes after me, and what is just, is not to be ... together, nor to be kept safe.

units.la: Ἐγὼ τούτῳ δίκαιον ἂν λόγον αὐτέπειμι; ὅπῃ καλῶς λέγεις, ὦ ἄνθρωπε, ἃ οἶδ' ἐν κινδύνῳ ὑπολογίζεσθαι τὸ ζῷ, ἢ τεθνάναι ἄνδρα, ὅτε πῃ καὶ σμικρὸν ὄφελος: ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐκεῖνο μόνον σκοπεῖν, ὅταν πέληται, πότερον δίκαιον ἢ ἄδικα, πέφευγε, καὶ αὖθις ἀγαθὸς ἢ κακός. Οὕτω δ' ἐχω ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι τῇ ἀληθείᾳ, ἐξ ἂν τις αὐτοὶ πάξῃ, ἢ γνοί[?]μένος ἐξελίσσειν, ἢ ὑπ' ἀρχόντων ταχθῇ, οὐ τοῖς ἀδει[?] ὡς ἐμοὶ δοκεῖ μένοντα κινδυνεύειν, μηδὲν ξυλλογιζόμενον, μήτε θάνατον, μήτε ἄλλο μηδὲν πρὸ τοῦ αἰσχροῦ.
units.tr: "Well said, my friend. But do you think a man of any worth should reckon the danger of living or dying, and not rather consider only this in his actions: whether he is doing right or wrong, and whether he is acting as a good man or a bad one? For truly, men of Athens, it is so: wherever a man has placed himself, or has been placed by his commanders, there, as it seems to me, he ought to stand and face danger, reckoning nothing of death or anything else before what is shameful."

units.la: Ἀλλ' ὦ μακάριε, ὅρα μὴ ἄλλο τι γενναῖον, καὶ ἀγαθὸν, ἢ σῴζειν τε καὶ σώζεσθαι. μὴ γὰρ ζῆν μέν, ὡς ζῷ ὅσον δὴ χρόνον, ἢ ὡς ἀληθῶς, ἀλλ' οὐ ἀδίκον ἐστὶν ὁ φιλοψυχητιόν, ἀλλ' ὠδὶ[?] ἐμφαίνειν πεῖ[?] τούτῳ τῷ Θεῷ, καὶ πισ[?]δοξοῦντα ταῖς γυναιξὶν, ὅπ τὴ εἰμαρμένῳ οὐδεὶς ἂν ἐκφύγοι. Τὸ ὠδὶ τύτῳ οἰκεῖον, πίνα ἂν τρόπον, Ἴσον ὃν μέλλει χρόνον ζῶναι, ὡς ἄεισα ζῶν. Περὶ σκοπεῖν ἄξιον δύμας, ὥσπερ συμπεριθέοντα· καὶ Ϲ τὰς τῶν στοιχείων εἰς ἄλληλα μεταβολὰς, συνεχῶς ἐννοεῖν. ἀφαιρεῖσθαι δὲ αἱ τύτην φαντασίαν, ἐν ἐμτὸν τῆ χαμαὶ βίου. Καλὸν δὲ τὸ Πλάτωνος· καὶ δὴ, πολὺ ἀνθρώπων τὸν λόγως ποιούμενον, ὡς ὀκνοπετεῖν δὲ καὶ τὰ ἐπίγεια, ὥσπερ τὸ ὄφιν ἀπωθὼν, κ᾽ ἀγέλας, στρατεύματα, γεωργίας, γάμους, διαλύσεις, γεννήσεις, θανάτους, δικαστηρίων θόρυβον, ἐρήμους χώρας, βαρβάρων ἔθνη ποικίλα, ἑορτὰς, θρήνους, ἀγορὰς, καὶ παμμιγεῖς· Ϲ δ᾽ ἐν τῷ συγκεκραμένον [?] τὰ πρόγεγονότα ἀναθεωρεῖν· τὰς τοσαύτας τῶν ἡγεμονιῶν μεταβολὰς, ἔξεστι καὶ τὰ ἑξόμενα προσφορᾶν. ὁμοιοδὴ γὰρ πάντως ἔσται, καὶ οὐχ οἷον τε ἐκεῖνα τὸ ῥυθμὸς τὴν νῦν γινομένων. ὅσον ἐν Ϲ ἰδὼν, δ᾽ πασταράκσυ[?]α ἕτεσιν ἱστορῆσαι ἐν ἀνθρώπινον βίον, τῷ ἐτῇ μύεια. τί δ᾽ τὸ λέοντα ὀλφ; καὶ τὰ ἐν γῆς μὲν φύντα, εἰς γαῖαν· τὰ δ᾽ ἀπ᾽ αὐθείας βλαστόντα γλίν, εἰς αὐθεῖον πάλιν ἡλθε πόλον. ἡ ὅτι δὲ διαλύσεις τὴν οἱ τοῖς ἀτόμοις ἀντεμαλοκῶν, καὶ τοιοῦτος πις σκεψασμὸς τ᾽ ἀπαθῶν στοιχείων.
units.tr: "But, my good friend, see whether there is anything else noble and good than to save and to be saved. For it is not right to love life merely as long as you live, or to care for it above all things, but to leave the outcome to God, and to trust the women's words, that no one can escape what is fated. Consider what is proper to this: however long a man is to live, let him live as he ought. Yet we should look at it as those who run beside us, and constantly think on the changes of the elements into one another. Turn your mind from that imagining and take away the fear of earthly life. Fine too is Plato's saying: he who speaks of many men, and of the things that are below, as if he were pushing away the swarm of... flocks, armies, farming, marriages, separations, births, deaths, the uproar of the law courts, deserted lands, the varied tribes of barbarians, feasts, lamentations, markets, and all things mixed together. Consider in the mixture the things that have gone before; the many changes of rulers can also be seen in what follows. For it will surely be the same, and it is not possible for them to be otherwise than the rhythm of what now happens. ..."

units.la: Καὶ σὶ Ζίσι, καὶ ὦτοις, ὁ μαγγανεύματαΠαρεκλέτουντες ὀχετὸν, ὥστε μὴ θανεῖν.Θεόθεν δὲ τινέουτ᾽ ἔρον, Ἀνάγκη τλῆναι, καμάζοις ἀνοδύρζοις.
units.tr: [Καὶ σὺ Ζεῦ, καὶ ὦτοις, ὁ μαγγανεύματα... ὥστε μὴ θανεῖν.] "And you, Zeus, and ... you who manage the arts of magic, so that you do not die. But it is a necessity from God to endure, and to lament and to weep."

units.la: [Οὐκ ἔστιν ἀρχὴ κακοῦ, ἀλλ᾽ τὸ ἀνωτάτω, τὴν πρὸς τῶν Πλατωνικῶν συναφὲς. Καθ[?]ἀλιώτερος, ἀλλ᾽ οὐχὶ κοινωνικώτερος, ἀδὲ αἱδημονέστερος, ἀδ᾽ ὕτακτότερος ὡδὶ ζῶις συμβαίνεσιν, ἢ ἢ ὑμβλνέστερ[?] πρὸς τὰ τ̄ πολιτικὰ προφάματα. Ὅπως ὀρῶν ἐ-πιμελείας διωαίζ[?], ἐχὶ τ̄ κοινὸν θεοῖς ἢ ἀνθρώποις λόγον, ἐκεῖ ἀδὲν δ᾽ φύον· ὅπως ὁ ἀφελείας τυχεῖν ἔξεσι, διὰ τ̄ ὁ δοσ σύσι, ἢ ἐπὶ τ̄ καταπολλὼ πο-ἰσοῦς ἀνεργείας, ἐκεῖ ἀδεμίαν βλέπω ὑφοράτι-ον. Ἀνάλαχος, ἢ διαγενεῖς σοί ὅτι ἐπὶ τὴν πρόσω συμβαίνει. Ἀ[?]οσκεῖς ὑμ[?] ἀρεσεῖν, ἢ ζῶις πρὸς τὴν ἀνθρώποις ἐπὶ δικαιοσωίλω προσφέρεαζ[?] ἐπὶ τὴν ἐ-σὴ φαντασίαν ἐμφιλοτεχνεῖν, ἵνα μήτι ἀκαταλλη-πτον πρόφορυ[?]. Μὴ ὠφελέπ[?] ἀλλότεια ἡγεμο-νικά[?]· ἀλλ᾽ ἐκεῖ βλέπε κατ᾽ ἐκεῖνο, ὡς πῶς ἡ φύσις ὁδηγεῖ, ἥτε τ̄ ὅλῳ, διὰ τ̄ συμβαινόντων ζοι, καὶ ἡ σὴ, διὰ τ̄ πεκτίων ἐπόδος. πρακτέον ἢ ἐνάσωμεν ἐξῆς τῇ καταπονδύῃ[?]. Καταπονδήσασθαι ἢ τὰ λοιπὰ, τ̄ λογικὸν ὀνέκαν, ὥσπερ ἢ ὡς ἀνθρώπους ἀλλ᾽, τὰ χείρω τ̄ κρεισσόνων ἕνεκεν, τὰ ἢ λογικὰ ἀλλήλων ἕνεκεν. Τὸ μὲν οὖν πεποι[?]ἡμένον, οὐ τῇ τ̄ ἀνθρώπῳ καταπονδύῃ, ἔ κοινωνικὸν ἐστί· δ᾽ οὖν[?]ρον δὲ, ἢ ἀνάσδον πρὸς τὰς σωματικὰς πέισεις. Λογικῆς δ᾽ ἢ νοερᾶς κινήσεως ἴδιον, πολιοςεί ζ[?]ν ἑαυτῷ, καὶ μὴ ποτε ἡ ἢ[?] ἀλλ᾽ μήτε αἰσθητικῆς μήτε ὁρμητικῆς κινήσεως· ζωώδες δ᾽ ἐκάτεραι, ἡ δὲ νοερὰ ἐλθὼν πρωτισθύειν, καὶ μὴ κα-τα-
units.tr: "There is no beginning of evil, but the highest, as the Platonists say. [He is] not more bitter, but not more sociable, nor more modest, nor more disciplined in the way that life is ordered, or more obedient to civic duties. Where I see care for what is common to gods and men, there I see nothing of it; where one may obtain benefit through the gift of nature, or through much labour, there I see nothing to be wondered at. ... Are you not pleased to be so? Or do you live toward the good of men, offering justice, and devising in your mind what can be rightly done, so that you never fall short? Do not regard others' guiding principles, but look at that alone, how nature leads, which is the whole, through the things that happen, and yours, through what is given. We must act, or else follow in order the suffering. Let us suffer what remains, the rational being for the sake of... as men, the worse for the sake of the better, the rational for the sake of one another. What has been made, then, is not social by the nature of man, but ..."

units.la: [The line ending "κα-τα-" is the last full line of the page, continued on the next page.] κἀτα κρατεῖσθαι ὑπ' ἐκείνων δικαίως γε. τὸ ἐπὶ φύκει γὰρ χρηστικὸν πᾶσιν ἐκείνοις. τεῖζον[?] οὖν τῇ λογικῇ κατασκευῇ τὸ ἀπρόπτωτον, ἢ ἀνεξαπάτητον. τοῦτ' οὖν ἐχόμενον δ' ἡγεμονικὸν, διὰ προαιρέτω, καὶ ἔχει τὰ ἑαυτῆς. Ὡς ἀχρτιθνή[?]κτά δὲ, καὶ μέχρι νῦν βεβιωκότα δ' λο[?]ίζων ἐν τῷ πολιόντᾳ, ζῆσαι, καὶ τῷ φύσιν, μόνον φιλεῖν τὸ ἑαυτῷ συμβαῖνον, καὶ συγκλωσθόμενον. τί γὰρ ἀρμόδιοτρον; ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ συμβάματι, ἐκείνους πρὸς ὁμμάτων ἔχειν, οἷς τὰ αὐτὰ συνέβαινεν· ἐπειτα ἤχθοντο, ἐξαίζοντο, ἐμέμφοντο· νῦν δὲ ἐκείνοι, ποῦ; οὐδαμοῦ. Τί ἂν δ σὺ λῇς ὁμοίως; οὐχὶ δ' ἐς τὰς μὲν ἀλλοτείας προπὰς καὶ τὰ λιπεῖν τοῖς τρέχουσι, ἡ τρεπομένοις; αὐτὸς δὲ, πολὺ τὸ πῶς χρῆσθαι αὐτοῖς ὅλῳ γίνεσθαι. χρήσῃ γὰρ καὶ λόγος, καὶ ὕλη σου ἔσου· μόνον πρόσεχε, καὶ φίλε σεαυτῷ καλὸς εἶν, ὃ παντὸς δ' πρόσεις, καὶ μέμνησο ἀμφοτέρων, ὅτι καὶ διάφορον, ἐφ' ᾧ ἡ πρᾶξις· ἔνδον βλέπει, οὐδὲν ἢ τυγχ' τῆς ἀγαθοῦ, καὶ ἀεὶ ἀναξλύειν δυναμέ-νη, ἐὰν ἀεὶ σκοπῆς· Δεῖ καὶ δ' σῶμα πεπιλιναι, καὶ μὴ διεσφίφθαι, μήτε ἂ κινήσει, μήτε ἂ χέσει. οἷον γὰρ ἡ ἰδίᾳ τὸ πρόσωπον πρέχει ἡ διάνοια, σωτὸν αὐτὸ καὶ ἂ δύχμου σωτηρούσα, τοιοῦτο καὶ ἰδί ὅλον τὸ σῶματ-τῷ ἀπαλητικόν, ὡς τὰ δὲ τῶν τα σὺ ὀρἀνεπιτηδεύτῳ φυλακτικά. Ἡ βιωτικὴ τῇ παιδευτικῇ ὁμοιότροπα, ἥπερ τῇ ὀρχηστικῇ· κ' δ', πρὸς τὰ ἐμπίπτοντα, καὶ οὐ προεγνωσμένα, ἑτοίμως καὶ ἁπλῶς ἐξᾶναι. Συνεχῶς ἐφίστασθαι, τινὲς εἰσὶν ἕτοιμοι, ὑφ' ὧν μαρτυρεῖσθαι θέλεις, καὶ τινα ἡγεμονικὴ ἐξουσία. ὅτε γὰρ μέμψῃ τοῖς ἀκουσίως πταίουσιν, οὔτε ἀμαρτυρήσεως δὴ σῇ, ἀ βλέπων εἰς τὰς πηγὰς τῆς ἐπιλήψεως καὶ ὀργῆς, αὐτὴν.
units.tr: "...be overcome by those justly, for by nature all those things are for use. So let us fortify the rational faculty against what cannot be stumbled over or deceived. Let this, then, be the ruling part held fast by choice, and let it hold what is its own. Having lived up to now, reckoning as one in the state, let us live, and by nature love only what happens to us and is woven with us. For what is more fitting? Against each happening, we should keep before our eyes those to whom the same things happened: then they were grieved, astonished, and blamed; but now where are they? Nowhere. What then do you wish to do? Do you not wish to leave to others what is theirs, and to those who run and turn, rather than to yourself? Yet the greater thing is how to use them, which is what makes the whole difference. For you will use both reason and matter, and you must attend to it, and be a friend to yourself, and remember both, that the act is different in kind: looking within, it will not fail to find the good, and it will always be able to correct itself if you keep watching. The body too must be kept in order and not be distorted, neither in movement nor in gesture. For just as the mind shows itself in the face, keeping it fixed and guarding it in good order, so too should the whole body be kept in its own form, as the art of fitness does. Life is like the art of training, which resembles dancing, for in what befalls us and is unforeseen we must be ready and simple. There are always ready at hand those by whom you are willing to be witnessed, and some ruling authority. For when you blame those who sin unwillingly, neither do you bear witness against yourself, looking to the sources of blame and anger."

units.la: Πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἄκουσα (φησιν) στέρεται ἀληθείας· ὅτας ὃν καὶ δικαιοσύνης, καὶ σωφροσύνης, καὶ ἀνδρείας, καὶ πάντως τῶν τοιούτων. ἀναγκαῖον δὲ, ὁ δ' ἡμέρας τοῦτον μεμνῆσθαι· ἔσῃ γὰρ πρὸς πάντας πρᾳότερος. ὠ μὲν πάντως πόνου, πρὸ-χειρον ἔσῳ, ὅτι ἂν ἀξιῶν, ὅδε τῶν διάνοιαν τὴν κυβερνωσαν, χείρω ποιεῖ. ὅτε γὰρ καὶ ὕλη ἐστὶν, ὅτι καὶ κοινωνική, διαφθείρει αὐτῷ. ὠδὶ μέντοι τῶν πλείστων τόνων, καὶ ὁ τῆς ἐπικούρου σοι βοηθεῖτω, ὅτι ὅτε ἀφόρησιν ὅτε εὐώνιον, ἐὰν τὴν ὀργὴν μνημονεύῃς, καὶ μὴ προσδεξάμενος. Ἐκείνου δὲ μέμνησο, ὅτι πολλὰ, τῶν ἃ αὐτὰ ὄντα, λανθάνει δύο χδαινόμενα. οἷον δ' ὑνυσάζειν, καὶ τὸ καὶ ματίζειαζ, καὶ τὸ ἀνοητικὸν. ὅταν ἐν τινι τύτῃ δυσαχεσῆς, λέγε ἑαυτῷ, ὅτι πόνῳ αἰδίδως. Ὅρα μή ποτε τοιοῦὂν πάσης πρὸς σὲ ἀπανθρώπους, δι' οἱ ἀνθρώ-
units.tr: Every soul is deprived of truth against its will, says he; and likewise of justice, temperance, courage, and all such things. It is necessary to keep this in mind, for you will be gentler toward everyone. Each of us is wholly in the grip of pain, and whoever, by his own judgment, makes the governing mind worse is harming himself. For this is his nature, and it is social. It is also the case that most people are kept from being harmed by the help of the reasoning faculty, and it helps you too: whether one is harmed or not depends only on whether you remember that anger does nothing good, and whether you refuse to be shaken by it. And remember this as well: many things, which are in themselves harmless, escape notice and are passed over in silence. When you are displeased with something, say to yourself, "I am giving way to ignorant pain." Take care lest, in your dealings with others, you become inhuman toward men, because of those things.

units.la: Note: the mark above and the margin note are read from the scan; sense is uncertain where the text is faint. ωσι[?] πρὸς τοὺς ἀνθρώπους. Ῥόθιον ἴσμεν, εἰ τηλαύ-γης Σωκράτης, καὶ διαλέξιν ἡρέασαν[?] ἦν. οὐ γὰρ ἀρκεῖ, εἰ Σωκράτης δυσδοξότερον ἀπέθανον[?], καὶ σὺ τρέχεσθαι τοῖς σοφισταῖς διελέγετο, μὴ καρτερικῶς τόρνον[?] σὺ τῷ πάγῳ διεννικτόρθυεν[?]· τὴν Σαλαμίνιον καλοῦνθεὶς ἄγειν, γενναιότερον ἔδοξεν ἀπιέναι, καὶ οὐ τοῖς ὁδοῖς ἐβρονάνετο[?]· πολὺ δὲ καὶ μάλις αὖ τῆς ἰδιώσεως, ἐπ᾽ ἀληθείας ἦν; ἀλλ᾽ ἐκεῖνο δὲ σκοπεῖν, ποίαν πινὰ τὴν ψυχὴν εἶχε Σωκράτης· καὶ ἐ ἰδιώσας ἀρ-κείας, τῷ δικαίῳ ἐν τὰ πρὸς ἀνθρώπους, ἢ ὅσιος τὰ πρὸς θεὸς, μήτε ἐκὴ πρὸς τὴν καινίαν ἀχανακτῆν[?], μηδὲ μὴ δ᾽ ἀλθὼν τινὸς ἀγνοίᾳ, μή τε τὴν ἀχρεμομένων ἐν τῷ ὅλῳ, ὡς ξένον, π δεχόμενος, ἢ ὡς ἀφόρητον ἐστιμένων, μήτε τοῖς τῶ συκευδίου πάθεσιν, ἐμπρέχων συμπαθῆ ὴν νοῦν.
units.tr: Note: the mark above and the margin note are read from the scan; sense is uncertain where the text is faint. Consider that we know Socrates was not a man of wealth, and that he was not in the habit of... For it is not enough that Socrates died in an ill-regarded way, while you go about disputing with the sophists; you must not endure with resolve the ... Going to the Salaminian (ship), he thought it nobler to depart, and did not ... Much more so, if it was truly a matter of his simplicity. But consider this: what kind of soul Socrates had. He was content with simplicity, with justice in his dealings with men and piety in his dealings with God, neither irritated by the ingratitude of others, nor ignorant of anything, nor accepting the things that happen in the whole as strange, or as intolerable, nor yielding to the passions of the body, but keeping his mind free and sympathetic.

units.la: Ἡ φύσις οὐχ ἕτως ἐωεκίρασε τῷ συγὠρίματα, ὡς μὴ ἐφεῖσθαι πολιορεί ζὴν ἑαυτόν, τὰ ἑαυτῆς ὑφ᾽ ἑαυτῷ, ποιεῖσθαι. λίαν γὰρ οὐδέ-χεται, θεὸν αὐτὸρ γεννᾶσθαι, καὶ ἐκ μηδενὸς γνωρισθῆναι. τοῦτο μὴ μένησο ἀεὶ, καὶ ἐπὶ ἐκείνου, ὅτι οὐ ὀλιγίσοις κεῖται, ἴ δυσκρυμένως βιῶ-σαι. καὶ μή, ὅπ ἀπίλπιστος διαλεκτικός, Φυσικὸς ἐσεαι, ἀλλ᾽ ὥσπερ ἀγραΐνως, ἡ ἐλεύθερος, ἢ ἀλήμων, καὶ κεινωνικὸς, καὶ δύπει ἡς θεῷ. Ἀ-ξιάσως δίζήσῃ[?], οὐ πολείσῃ θυμηδίας, καὶ ἀν τοῦτοὺς καταιδέσῃ[?], ἄπινα βλάπτουσι, κἂν τὰ ἡ-εἰκ διαπᾶς[?] τὰ μελύδεια[?], τῇ πολιτευομένῳ[?] τούτῳ φυράματι[?]. πῶς κωλύσῃ πᾶσι τὰς διανοίας σῴζειν ἑαυτῶν, οὐ γαληνήν, ὁ κείος[?] τῇ πρὸς τὴν ἀδυναμίαν[?] τὴν ἀλήθειαν, καὶ χρήσει τὴν ἐπισκεδαμμένων ἑτοίμην; ὥστε τῷ μὲν κείσιν λέγειν τῷ πεποιηκότι, ἐὰν ὑπάρχεις κατ᾽ οὐσίαν, κἂν ἐξ ἕξεως ἄλλοιον φαίνῃ; τῷ δὲ χρήσιν λέγειν τῷ πεποιηκότι, σε ἐξήτου. ἀεὶ γὰρ μοι τὸ πρὸν, ὕλη ἀρετῆς λογικῆς ἢ πολιτικῆς· καὶ τὸ ζῷον, τέχνης ἀνθρώπου ἢ θεοῦ. πᾶν γὰρ τὸ συμβαῖνον, ἡ ἡ ἀνθρώπῳ, ἡ ἡ οἰκῇ[?], ὅτε καινόν, ὅτε δυσμεταχείριστον, ἀλλὰ γνώριμον καὶ ἐνεργές. Τοῦτο ἔχει ἡ τελειότης τῆς ἡδονῆς, τὸ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν, ὡς τελευταίαν, διεξάγειν, καὶ μήτε σφύζειν, μήτε ναρκᾶν, μήτε συμπεπείνεσθαι. Οἱ θεοί, ἀθάνατοι ὄντες, οὐ δυσχεραίνουσιν, ὅτι εἰ τοσοῦτῳ αἰῶνι, δήποτε αὐτὸν, πάντως ἀεὶ τοιοῦτον ὄντα, καὶ τοσοῦτον φύλαξιν, ἀνέχεσθαι. Προσέτι δὲ καὶ ἡδονται αὐτῇ ταυτοίως. οὐ δέ ὄσον οὐδὲ πω λέγειν μέλλοντος ἀπαυδᾶς, καὶ τοῦτο ἐτοῖς ὧν τὴν φυλαγην. Γελοῖόν ἐστι, τῷ μὲν ἰδίαν καὶ κίαν μὴ φύγειν, ὃ καὶ δυνατὸν ἐστι· τῷ δὲ τὴν ἄλλως φεύγειν, ὅπερ ἀδύνατον. Ὃ ἂν ἡ λογικὴ καὶ πολιτικὴ δύναμις ἐξοίκῃ, μήτε νεοφὸν, μή τε
units.tr: Nature has not so mingled the elements that a man should be unable to besiege himself and make his own things subject to himself. For it is certainly not allowed that a god should be born from nothing and be recognised. Keep this in mind always, and keep in mind that it lies in your power to live without grief. Do not be a dialectician without the spirit of a natural man; rather be like a free man, or a wanderer, and social, and obedient to God. Live in a worthy way; you will not be deprived of joy, even if you are ashamed of those who harm them, even if you fail to ... the things that are in your power, in this mixture which is subject to change. How will you prevent all men from keeping their minds, not in tranquillity, but in an unfeigned truth as to their weakness, and using, as ready to hand, what has been scattered? Thus, to the one who made the thing, one may say: "If you are in your essence, whatever you may appear to be by your condition, what you wished for..." and to the one who made the use, one may say: "I sought you." For the matter of reason, or of political virtue, is always before me; and the living creature is the art of man or of God. For everything that happens is either from man or from the things of the house; it is not new, nor hard to manage, but familiar and active. This is the perfection of pleasure: to pass through each day as if it were the last, and to be neither agitated nor numbed nor pretending. The gods, being immortal, are not vexed that they must bear for so long a time a being who is always such, and so guarded. Moreover, they also delight in it in the same way. Do not, then, shrink from one who is about to speak, nor from this... Those who are nothing should be ashamed to flee their own nature, which is possible, but to flee another's, which is impossible. Whatever the rational and political power dwells in, is neither new nor...

units.la: [The Greek is printed in a cursive-style face and is only partly legible on the scan. The reading above is provisional; words marked [?] are doubtful.] κοινωνικὸν, οὐλότως κατὰ δεύτερον ἑαυτῆς κείμενον. Ὅταν οὖν ὃ τε ποιητικὸς ᾖς, καὶ ἄλλῳ οὖ τε ποιοῦντας, τί ἐπὶ ζητεῖς τέταρτον πρὸς τῶν πε[?], ὥσπερ οἱ μορφοὶ, καὶ δόξαι οὖ πεποιηκέναι, ἢ τὸ ἀμοιβῆς τυχεῖν. Οὐδεὶς κάμνει ὠφελεῖσθαι, ὠφέλιμα κατὰ φύσιν. μὴ ἓν κάμνε ὠφε-λύμενον, ᾧ ᾧ ὠφελεῖς. Ἡ τὸ ὅλον φύσις ὡδὲ πλὴν κοσμοποιῆσαι ὥρμησεν. νῦν ἤ, ἢ τοι ὡς ἀεὶ γινόμενον κατ' ἐπακολούθησιν γίνεται, ἢ ἀλόγισα καὶ τὰ κινεώτατά ἐστιν, ἐφ' ἃ ποιεῖται ἰσχὺν ὁρμῶν, δι' τὸ κόσμου ἡγεμονικόν. εἰς πολλὰ σε γαλιωότροπος ποιήσει, ὥσπερ μνημο-νευόμενον.
units.tr: Since you have both the active cause and the material on which it works, why look for a fourth thing beyond these, as the foolish do, expecting either the credit of having done something or a return for it? No one should labour to be helped in a way contrary to nature. The nature of the whole set out to make a world. Either whatever happens comes about by an unbroken sequence, as it always does, or the things most essential are those toward which the governing reason of the universe directs its strength. In many ways it will make you turn about, as one who remembers.

units.la: ΜΆΡΚΟΥ ἈΝΤΩΝΙ-ΝΟΥ αὐτοκράτορος, τῶν εἰς ἑαυ-τὸν βιβλίων η´.
units.tr: The Meditations of Marcus Antoninus, Emperor, Book 8.

units.la: [?]Αἱ γὰρ πρὸς τὸ ἀκενόδοξον φύ-σει, ὅτι ἐν ἐπὶ διώκειν τὸν βίον ὅλον, ἢ τὸν γε ἀρχὴ νεότητος φιλοσόφου βιβλιωκέναι· ἀλλὰ πολλοῖς τε ἄλλοις, καὶ αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ δῆλος γέγονας, πόρρω φιλοσοφίας ὤν· τί φυγεῖν ἔν, ὥστε τῷ μὲν δόξαν τῷ τὸ φι-λοσόφῳ λοξόφου κτήσασθαι, ὅκέπι σοι ῥάδιον: αὐτ[?]νίζεται δὲ καὶ ἡ ὑπόληψις. ἐπὶ ὃν ἀληθῶς ἑώρακας, τοῦ κέτα[?] πρᾶγμα, ὃ μὲν τὴ δόξης, ἄφες· ἀρκιόθητι δὲ, ἐ κἂν ὃ λοιπὸν τῆς βίου, ὅσον ἂν ποτε ἡ σὴ φύσις θέλει, βιώσεν. καὶ πανόησον ἂν τί θέλει, καὶ ἄλλο μηδὲν πάσιαν[?]τω. πεπείρασαι γὰρ, πόλι τόσου τὰ ἀλυνηθεὶς, ἰδ. ἀμὸς ἂν ἔχε ὅ ἂν ζῇ. ἐν οἷ συλλογισμοῖς, ἐν οἷ πλούτῳ, οὐκ οἷ δόξῃ, οὐκ οἷ ἀχρλαύσει, οὐδαμοῦ· τοῦ ἂν ἔσεν; οἷ ἡ ποιεῖν, ἀ ἐ ἱ ζ[?]- τεῖ ἢ τῆς ἀνθρώπων φύσις. πῶς ἂν ταῦτα ποιήσει; ἐπαν δόγματα ἔχῃ ἀφ᾽ ὧν οἷ ὁρμαὶ καὶ οἷ πράξεις. τίνα δόγματα; τὰ τοῦ ἀγαθῶν, καὶ κακῶν. ὡς οὐδενὸς μὲν ἀγαθὸν ὄντος ἀνθρώ-πῳ, ὃ οὐχὶ ποιεῖ δίκαιον, σώφρονα, ἀνδρεῖον, ἐλεύθερον· ὅδ᾽ ἑνὸς δὲ κακῶν ὃ οὐχὶ ποιεῖ ταχὺ πέρ τοῖς ἐρημίαις. Καθ᾽ ἑκάστων πρᾶξιν ἐρώτα σεαυτὸν, πῶς μοί αὕτη ἔχει; μὴ μεταγνώσῃ ἐπ᾽ αὐτῇ; μικρὸς καὶ τέθνηκα, καὶ πάντ᾽ ἐν μέσῳ· τί τὸ λοιπὸν ἀληθῶς, ἐ δ᾽ ποὺ ὄρῳ, ζῷου νοερου, καὶ κοινωνικοῦ, καὶ ἱεροῦ[?] νόμῳ θεῷ. Ἀλέξανδρος δὲ, καὶ Γάϊος, καὶ Πομπήϊος, τί πρὸς Διογένην, καὶ Ἡράκλειτον, ἢ Σωκράτην; οἱ μὲν γὰρ εἶδον τὰ πράγματα, καὶ τὰς αἰτίας, ἢ τὰς ὕλας, καὶ τὰ ἡγεμονικὰ ἐν αὐτῇ τοῦ τί. ἐκεῖ δὲ ὅσων προνοῖα, καὶ δελέα ἀλλέα τοσῶν, ὅτι οὐδὲν ἧττον τὰ αὐτὰ ποιήσουσι, κἂν σὺ διαῤῥαγῇς. Τὸ πρῶτον μὲν ταράσσ[?]εται· πάντα γὰρ ἐν τῷ τῆς ὅλου φύσει[?], καὶ ὀλίγου χρόνου, ὀδὲς ἀλαμῶν ἔσῃ, ὥσπερ δὲ Ἀδριανὸς, ὀδὲ Αὔγυστος[?].
units.tr: For the one who is not concerned with vainglory, it is enough that he has not pursued his whole life in this way, or at least has not spent the early years of his youth in philosophy. You have shown yourself to many others and to yourself that you are far from philosophy, so it is hard for you to gain the reputation of a philosopher. Let go of this hope of glory, and be content to live the rest of your life as far as your nature wills. Consider what it wants, and seek nothing else. You have tried many things and failed to find what you sought: not in syllogisms, not in wealth, not in reputation, not in pleasure, nowhere. Where then is it? In doing what human nature requires. How will you do this? By holding to the principles from which impulses and actions arise. What principles? Those concerning good and evil: that nothing is good for a man which does not make him just, temperate, brave and free, and nothing is evil which does not make him the opposite. Ask yourself with regard to every action: how does this stand with me? Will I regret it? I shall soon be dead, and all things will be gone. What then is still to be sought, if not to act as a rational and social living being, obeying the same law as God? Alexander, Gaius and Pompey, what are they compared with Diogenes, Heraclitus or Socrates? These men knew the things themselves, their causes and their matter, and their governing reason. But as for them, how many cares and dependences on others they had! Those men will do the same whether you are harmed or not. First, do not be disturbed, for all things are in accordance with the nature of the whole, and within a short time you will be no one, just as Hadrian and Augustus are no one.

units.la: ἔπειτα, ἀτονίσας εἰς τὸ πρᾶγμα, ἴδε αὐτό, καὶ συμνημονεύσας, ὅτι ἀγαθὸν σε ἄνθρωπον εἶναι δεῖ, ὅ τί τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἡ φύσις ἀπαιτεῖ, πᾶξον ζῶσῳ ἀμετατρεπί[?], καὶ ἑτοίμως ὡς δικαιότατον φαίνεταί σοι, μόνον ὑμένως, καὶ αἰδημόνως, ὦ ἀνυποκείτως.
units.tr: Then, fixing your attention on the matter, look at it closely, and remember that you ought to be a good man, and what human nature requires. Do it without deviation, and say what seems most just to you, but do so gently, modestly and without hypocrisy.

units.la: Ἡ τῶν ὅλων φύσις ζῷον ὅρον ἔχει[?], τὰ ὧδε ὄντα, ἐκεῖ μετατίθεσθαι, μεταβάλλειν, αἴρειν ἀφθον[?], καὶ ἐκεῖ φέρειν. Πάντα τρόπαι, οὐχ ὥστε φο-βεῖσθαι, μήτι καινόν· πάντα σωθήση[?]· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἴσου αἱ ἀφεμεμήσεις. Ἀρκεῖ δὲ πᾶσα φύσις, ἑαυτῇ ἀύσ ἐστι[?]. Φύσις ἡ λογικὴ, ἀὐσθεῖ, ἐὰν μὴ φαντάσιας, μήτε φθείρηται, μήτε ἀδήλῳ, συγκαταπθεμένη[?]· τὰς ὁρμὰς ὃ, ὧδὶ τὰ κοινωνικὰ ὄντα μόνα, ἀπθυθύνεσθαι[?]· τὰς ὀρέξεις δὲ, καὶ τὰς ἐγκλίσεις, τὰ ἐφ᾽ ἡμῖν, μόνον πεποιημένη[?]· ὁ δὲ, ἐν τῇ κοινῇ φύσεως ἀφηρημένον, πᾶν ἀσαλομέ-νη[?]. μέρος δ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν[?]· ὡς ἡ τοῦ φύλου φύσις, τῇ τοῦ φυτοῦ φύσεως. ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι, ἐκεῖ μὴ, ἡ τοῦ φυλλοῦ φύσις, μέρος δὲ φύσεως, καὶ ἀναισθήτου, ἢ ἀλόγου, καὶ ἐμπολιζεσθαι δυναμένης· ἡ δὲ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου φύσις, μέρος δὲ ἀνεμπολίστου φύσεως. σεως, καὶ νοερᾶς, καὶ δικαίας· εἰ γε ἴσως, καὶ κατ' ἀξίαν, εὖ μερισμὸς, χρόνων, οὐσίας[?], αἰτίου, αἰτίας, συμβάσεως, ἐνίοις[?] ποιεῖται. σκοπῷ δὲ, μὴ ἐπὶ τὸ πρὸς τὸ οὐ ἴσον δυνήσεις ἐπὶ πάν-τας· ἀλλ' εἰ συμμέλειν τὰ πάντα· τῇ δὲ πρὸς ἀθρόα, τὰ τῇ ἑτέρᾳ ἀναγινώσκειν ἐξεστιν· ἀλ-λὰ ὕβειν ἀνέργειν ἐξεστιν, ἀλλὰ ἡδονῶν καὶ τῶνων καὶ ἀντιπροτρέπειν ἐξεστιν· ἀλλὰ τῇ δοξαείου ὑπεράνω ἐν ἐξεστιν· ἀλλὰ ἀναισθήτοις καὶ ἀχαρεῖσοις μὴ συμᾶσθαι, πῶς οὖν κίνδυνος αὐ-τὴν ἐξεσιν. μηκέτι σου μηδὲς ἀκύσῃ καὶ τὰ μεμφομένης τὸν οὖ αὐλῇ βίον· μηδὲ τὴν σεαυτῷ. Ἡ με-πίνοια, ὅσιν ἐπίληψίς τις ἑαυτῷ, ὡς χρησίμου τι πράγματι. τὸ δὲ ἀγαθὸν, χρήσιμόν τι δεῖ εἶν, ἢ ἐπιμελητέον αὐτῷ τῷ ἀγαθῷ καὶ καλῷ αἰδεῖ. οὐδὲς δ᾽ ἂν καλὸς καὶ ἀγαθὸς αὐτῆς μετανοή-σειεν, ὡδὶ τῷ ἡδονῷ, πνα πρέπει. ὅτι ἄρα χρήσιμον, ὅτι ἀγαθόν, ἡδονή. ὅρα τί ἐστιν αὐτὸ καθ' ἑαυτὸ τὴν ἰδίαν καταςκευήν; τί μὲν τὸ ὑσιῶ-δες αὐτῆς, καὶ ὑλικὸν; τί δὲ τὸ αἰτιῶδες; τί δὲ ποιεῖ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ; πόσον δὲ χρόνον ὑφίσαται; Ὅταν ἐξ ὕπνου δυσχερῶς ἐγέρῃ, ἀναμιμνή-σκων, ὅτι ἐπὶ τῶν καταςκευῶν ἐστι, καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ ἀνθρωπικῷ φύσιν, ὅ' πράξις κοινωνικὰς ἀφιδύνασθαι. τὸ δὲ καθ' ἓν, κοινὸν καὶ τὴν ἀλόγων ζώων. ὃ δὲ κατὰ φύσιν ἐκάσῳ, ὅτοφ εἰκειότερον καὶ προσφυέστερον, καὶ δὴ καὶ πει-σινέστερον · διηνεκῶς, καὶ ὡδὶ πάσης ἐ οἷόν τε, φανταστίας. Φυσιολογεῖν, παθολογεῖν, Διαλεκτικὸν εἶναι, ᾧ ἂν αὐτυγχάνῃς σὺν τῷ πόλει; ἔστι, τίνα δόγματα ἔχει περὶ ἀγαθῶν ἢ κακῶν; ἢ περὶ ἡδονῆς καὶ τῶν [?] ἡδονικῶν ἑκατέρας, καὶ περὶ δόξης, ἀδοξίας, θανάτου, ζωῆς. Διαὶ δὲ τινα δόγματα ἔχειν ἐν θαυμασὸν, ἢ ξένον μοι δόξῃ, ἐὰν τὸ ὃ τινα ποιῇ. Μεμνήσομαι, ὅτι ἀναγκάζει ὅτως ποιεῖν. Μέμνησο, ὅτι ὥσπερ αἰ χρόνον ξενίζεσθαι, ἡ ἡσυχῇ σῦκα φέρει, ὅτως ἡ ὁ κόσμος τὰ δέ τινα φέρει, ὧν ὅτι φορός.
units.tr: The nature of the whole has its limit: the things here are to be changed and transformed, and then carried elsewhere into another state. Everything is according to a fixed order and a turning of the same things. Do not be afraid of anything new, for all things are familiar. Every nature is content with itself, and the rational nature is sufficient for itself, if it is not corrupted by imagination and does not wander from what is according to nature. It is able to direct its impulses only towards what is social, and to devote its desires and aversions only to what is in our power. What belongs to the common nature it accepts as its own, as the part of a plant does not differ from the nature of the whole plant. But the nature of the plant is not reasoning, and is not free to fail; the nature of man is a part of the nature that is free from such hindrance. And the nature of man is part of the rational and just nature; for in some way and by proportion, the division of time, substance, cause, and the chance of events is made by it. Do not look to what is unequal, but consider whether everything is in harmony. You may not be able to make an equal distribution to all, but you can be content with the one who has been given something. Yet it is not permitted to be carried away by pleasure, nor to be at ease in pain, nor to be indifferent to glory, nor to be troubled by the insensible and ungrateful. How then can one fall into danger? Do not let your mind be consumed by anything, nor let your life be spent in anger or flattery. Remember that the mind is a kind of self-possession, which keeps itself as something useful. The good must be useful, or else it must be cared for as good and beautiful for its own sake. No one who is good and beautiful will regret such a thing. Remember that what is useful is good and that pleasure is not. See what it is in itself, and what its substance and material are, what is its cause, what it does in the world, and how long it lasts. When you rise unwillingly from sleep, remind yourself that you are made for acting as a human being, for working with others. What is common is also shared with the unreasoning animals. What is according to nature belongs to each one, and is more fitting and suitable. And again, you are able to consider every imagination constantly, in no way. To be a student of nature, a student of the passions, a dialectician: for whatever you happen to be doing with the city, consider what opinions it holds about good and evil, or about pleasure and pain, and about glory, dishonour, death and life. It is no wonder if it holds these opinions, or if they seem strange to me when it acts accordingly. Remember that it is compelled to act so. Remember that as the fig tree in its season bears figs, so the world bears what it bears, and of this some are useful.

units.la: ἰατρῷ ἢ ἡ κυβερνήτῃ, αὐχὸν ξενίζεσθαι, ἐ πεπύρεχον ὅτι, ἢ ἐ αὐτὴ πνοια γίγονται. Μέμνησο ὅτι μετα πίπτειν, ὃ ἔπεσθαι δὲ διορθοῦντι, ὁμοίως ἐλθὼ ἱερόν ἐστι. οὐ γὰρ ἐνέργεια, καὶ τῷ ζῶ ὁρμῶ, ἐ ὡς ἐμὶ ἕν, νοῦν δ' ἐν σοὶ, πρᾶν ὁμολογῶ ἐ πολλοὺς ἡ, ἐ ὡς ἐπ' ἄλλῳ, τίνι μέμφη; τοῖς ἐπόμβης, ἢ τοῖς θεοῖς; ἀμφότερα μακαρίως · ὠδὲ μεμπτέον. ἐὰν ἐ γὰρ διώκῃ, διορθωτέον πῶς αὐτό· ἐ ὃ ἐσ οὐ μὴ διώκω, πρὸς τί ἐπὶ σοὶ φέρει τὸ μέμφεσθαι; ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἀδελ ποιητέον. Ἐξω τὸν κόσμον δ' ἀχρεῖόν οὐ πίπτει. ἐὰν ὧδε μένει μεταβάλλει, ὧδε ἐ ἀλλάττεται ἐς τὰ ἱερά, ἃ στοιχεῖά ἐστι τοῦ κόσμου, ἡ σά.
units.tr: To a doctor or a pilot it is not strange that some are dismissed, and he himself did not yet have the power to set things right. Remember that to fall is not shameful, and to set oneself right is also no shame. For there is an activity and a living impulse in you, not separate from the mind in you, which you yourself acknowledge many do not have. Of what then do you complain? Is it the things that come, or the gods? Both are blessed, and neither is to be blamed. If anything is not done rightly, it must be corrected by you; if you do not pursue it, what right do you have to find fault? For the world has no unfortunate thing that falls outside of it. Whatever remains is changed, and whatever is changed is not destroyed into the things that are the elements of the world, which are also in it.

units.la: ἀ] Eight words of this note are unclear; see notes. καὶ αὐτὰ δὲ μεταβάλλει, καὶ οὐ γογγύζει. ἕκαστον πρός τι γίγονεν, ἵππῳ[?], ἀμπέλῳ[?], τί θαυμάζεις; καὶ ὁ ἥλιος ἐρεῖ, πρὸς τὸ ὄμμα[?] γίγονα, καὶ οἱ λίθοι θεοί. σὺ δὲ πρός τί; τὸ ἡδύ; ἴδε ἡ ἀνέχεται ἡ ἔννοια. ἡ φύσις ἔσχα[?]σται ἑαυτόν· οὐδὲν ἐλάσσον τῆς ἀρχῆς[?], ἢ τῆς ἀρχῆς τε καὶ διεξαγωγῆς. ὡς ὁ ἀναβαλλόμενος τὴν σφαῖραν· τί οὖν ἀγαθόν, ὡς σφαιρίῳ ἀναφερομένῳ, ἢ καὶ νῦν, καὶ ἀφεροµένῳ, ἢ καὶ πεπωκότι; τί δὲ ἀγαθόν, τῇ τοῦ μφόλυγι ζωῇ, ἢ καὶ νῦν, ἀλαλυθείᾳ[?]; τὰ ὅμοια ὁ καὶ ὡς λύχνος. ἐκ-ζεόν, καὶ διαχέα, οἷον ὅτι, γηραλέον ὁ οἷον γίνεται, νοσοῦν ὁ, τορνεύων, βραχύβιον ὁ; ἢ ὁ ἐπαινῶν, ἢ ὁ ἐπαινούμενος, καὶ ὁ μνημονεύων, καὶ ὁ μνημονευόμενος· ποσότι δὲ καὶ οἱ γονία τοῦτον τῷ κλίματι· καὶ οὐδὲ οἱ τῶν ἁπάντες συμφωνοῦσι, καὶ οὐδὲ αὐτὸς τὶς ἐαυ-τοῦ· καὶ ὅλη δὲ ἡ ἡγὴ σιγμή. πόσον ἐχε τῷ νῦν πα-κειμένῳ, ἢ τῷ δήγματι, ἢ τῇ ἐνεργείᾳ, ἢ τῷ ἡμαινομένῳ. δίκαιος τῶν πάντα πάσχεις. μᾶλλον ἡ Ἡλίος ἀγαθὸς αὔειον γίνεσθε, ἡ σήμερον ἔν. πάσω τί; πάσω ἐπ' ἀνθρώπων δύναμιν ἀναφέρων. συμβαίνει τί μοι; δέχομαι, ὡς θεὸς ἀναφέρων, καὶ πῶς τὴν αὐτὴν πηγὴν, ἀφ' ἧς πάντα τὰ γινόμενα συμμηνεῖται. ὅ τοῦτο σοι φαίνεται δ' λέγεις; ἕλαιον, ἰσχρῶς, ξύπτ, ὕδωρ, γλαθιῶδες, παὶ τα σιηχαυῖα. τοιοῦτον παῦ μέρος τ̃ βίυ, ἡ παῦ ὑποκέιμενον. Λύκιλλα Οὐήρον, εἶτα Λύκιλλα Σεκύνδα, Μάξιμον· εἶτα Σεκύνδα, ὡδὶ τύγχανΘ Διόπιμον, εἶτα ὡδὶ τύγχανΘ Φωσίναν, Αντωνῖνον. εἶτα Αντωνῖνο τοιαῦτα παῦτα. Κέλερ, Αδελιανόν· εἶτα Κέλερ. οἱ ῷ δελιμᾶς ἐκεῖνο, ἢ προγνωστικοί, ἢ τετυφωμένοι, ὧ; οἷον δελιμᾶς μὲν, χάρᾱξ καὶ Δημήτριος ὁ Πλατωνικός, Εὐδαίμων, καὶ εἴτις τοιοῦτο· παῦτα ἐφήμερα, τεθνηκότα πάλαι. οἱ μὲν γὰρ εὶς ἐπ' ὀλίγον μνημονευθέντες· οἱ δ' εἰς μύθος μετα βαλόντος· οἱ δὲ ἢ ἀδη καὶ ἐκ μύθων ἐξίτηλοι. τούτων οὖν μεμνῆσθ, ὅτι δεῖ σε ἢ τοι σκεδασθῆναι τὸ συγκριμάτιόν σου, ἢ σβεσθῆναι δ' ἀνθρώπου, ἢ μετασῆναι, καὶ ἀλλαχῦ καὶ τα τα χθῆναι. ὑψροζωὴ ἀνθρώπου, ποιεῖν τὰ ἴδια ἀνθρώπου. Ἴδιον ἡ ἀνθρώπου, δύνοια πρὸς τὸ ὁμόφυλον, ὑπόρρῳσις τῶν αἰσθητικῶν κινήσεων, διαλύρισις τῶν πιθανῶν φαντασιῶν, ἐδιεπιώρησις τ' τὴν ὅλην φύσεως, ©τ' κατ' αὐτὴ γινομένων. Ζῆς ἐέσεις· ἢ μὲν πρὸς τὸ αὔπον δ' τὸ ἐκεῖνο ὑποιμένον· ἢ ἡ πρὸς τὴν θέαν αὐτὴν, ἀφ' ἧς συμβαίνῃ πᾶσιν πᾶν̈ζα· ἢ ἡ πρὸς σὺν συμβιῶντας. Ὁ πόν, ἢ τοι ζῷ σώματι καλόν, ὅσον ἀχρφαινέσθω, ἢ τῇ ψυχῇ. Διὰ ἔξεσιν αὐτῇ, πῶς ἰδίαν αὐθρίαν, καὶ χαλήνλω, διαφυλάσσῃ, καὶ μὴ
units.tr: The things themselves change and do not grumble. Everything is made for something: the horse, the vine, why do you wonder? The sun will say: I was made for this. The stones too are gods. But you, for what? For pleasure? Look whether reason tolerates this. Nature has set itself in order; nothing is less than its beginning or its middle or its end. Like the one who throws a ball, what good is there in the ball rising, or falling, or being struck, or even fallen? What good is there in the bubble's life, whether it lasts or bursts? Things are similar as with a lamp: when it is ignited and when it flickers and fails, what does it become? Whether old or sick or sharpened, what does it become? Whether the one who praises or the one who is praised, and the one who remembers or the one who is remembered, all are of this kind. Nor do the people of the regions agree among themselves, nor even does each one agree with himself. The whole of life is a moment. Consider the substance of what lies before you, or of the pain, or of the action, or of what is disturbed. Just as with the sun, the good thing becomes more beautiful at evening than at morning. What is it that I am doing? I receive what comes, as a god, and I refer it to the source from which all things that happen come. What do you say this is? Oil, cheese, flies, water, a dung-heap, and all such things. Such is the part of life, and of the one who lies beneath it. Lucilla, Verus, then Lucilla, Secunda, Maximus, then Secunda, Diotimus, then Fortunatus, Antoninus, then Antoninus, all such. Celer, Hadrianus, then Celer. Those who were famous, or prophetic, or conceited, where are they? For example, Charax and Demetrius the Platonist, Eudaemon, and any such: these were ephemeral and died long ago. Some were remembered only briefly, others have become a myth, and others are wholly forgotten even among myths. Remember, then, that you must either be scattered, the compound that you are, or the breath of life must be extinguished, or it must be moved and carried elsewhere. The proper work of a human being is to do what is proper to humanity: love for those of the same kind, contempt for the movements of sense, discrimination of plausible appearances, and contemplation of the whole of nature and of what happens in accordance with it. Three relations are yours: one to the body that encloses you, another to the divine cause from which all things come, and a third to those who live with you. Whatever happens to the body, let it be as good as it can be made; and to the soul, let it be kept as its own, and guarded so that it does not take up any opinion without judgement.

units.la: ἔπεθἐπολαμβάνειν ὁπωσοῦν. πᾶσα κρίσις, ὁρ-μὴ, καὶ ὄρεξις, ἔκκλισις, εἴδωλον, καὶ οὐδὲν κακὸν ὧδε ἀναβαίνει. Ἐξάλειφε τὰς φαντασίας, (ᾧ-) χῶς σεαυτῷ λέγων· νῦν ἐπ' ἐμοί ἐστιν, ἵνα μὴ ταύτῃ τῇ ψυχῇ μηδεμία τυραννίς ᾖ, μηδὲ ὠδὶ ὀργὴ ... ταραχὴ πρὸς ἅπαντα βλέπων τὰ σωματικὰ ἐστιν, χρῶμαι ἑκάστῳ κατ' ἀξίαν, μένω τῆς οὐσίας, καὶ φύσιν λαλεῖν, ἧ οὐ συγκλίνω, ὃ πρὸς πάντ' ὀνπνεῖ, ἠρεμίως. μὴ τοῖς λαμβάνων λόγῳ χρῆσθαι. Αὐλὴ Αὐγύστῃ, γυνὴ, Ἰουλιάτης, ἐγγονοι, πρόγονοι, ἀδελφὴ, Ἀγρίππας, συγγενεῖς, οἰκεῖοι, φίλοι, Ἄρφος, Μαικήνας, ἰατροί, ἀλλ' ὅλης αὐλῆς Ἀτόνατος. εἶτα ἐπιθὲ τὰς ἄλλας, μὴ καθ' ἕνος ἀνθρώπῳ θάνατον· οἷον Πομπηΐων, κἀκεῖνο ὃ ἀνθρεσφόμενον τοῖς μνήμασιν, ἑκάτος τῇ ἰδίᾳ γένους ἀνθλοιἰζεσθαι. τόσα ἐσπαλαθήσαν οἱ πρὸ αὐτῶν, ἵνα διαλθεχὸν ἵνα καταλίπωσιν· εἶτα, ἀνάγκη ἑκατὸν ἵνα γενέσθαι. πάλιν ὧδε ὅλα γένους θάνατον, ζῶν δὲ ... τὸν βίον, καὶ μίαν πεῖξιν· καὶ εἰ ἐκφύση, τὸ ἑαυτὸ πῖ ἔχει, ὡς οἷόν τε, ἀρκεῖσθαι. ἵνα δὲ τὸ ἑαυτὸ ἀσθένη, ὧδε εἰς σε κωλύσει δώσει. ἀλλὰ σὺ σαυτοῦ τί ἐξωθεν; οὐδὲν, εἰς γε τὸ δικαίως, καὶ Σωφρόνως, καὶ βουλεύεσθαι. ἄλλο δὲ λέ ἴσως ἐνεργικὸν κωλυθήσεται; ἀλλὰ τῇ πρὸς αὐτὸ τὸ κώλυμα διαρεσήσει, καὶ τῇ ὧδὶ τὸ διδόμενον δύγνώ-
units.tr: ...to grasp them in any way at all. Every judgement, impulse, desire and aversion, and every image of evil, is cast out, and no evil arises from them. Wipe out your impressions by saying to yourself: "It is in my power that no wickedness or tyranny should be in this soul, and that I should be neither angry nor disturbed about anything." Look at all bodily things, use each according to its worth, and remain calm towards what is not in your power. Consider Augusta, her wife, Julia, grandchildren, ancestors, sister, Agrippa, kinsmen, household, friends, Arius, Maecenas and physicians: the whole court is dead. Then turn to the others, and consider not one man's death but the death of whole families. Pompeius, and whatever is inscribed on the tombs, each perished in his own time. Those who came before them struggled to leave something behind, and yet they too were compelled to die. So consider the death of the whole race, and that life is only a single moment. If you see this, be content with what your own nature allows you to take. And if someone hinders you, let no one prevent your mind from being at rest; the hindrance is only of the body. But what is it that hinders you from acting justly, soberly and prudently? If something outside stands in the way of some action, turn that very obstacle to good use: the action is then changed into another, which fits the design, and so it is accepted without pride and pursued without hesitation.

units.la: Note: the scan is faint and partly illegible in the marginal and Greek text. Readings marked as partly guessed should be checked against the original. ἀγνώμονι μεταβάλοσι, οὕτως ἄλλη πρᾶξις αὐ-τὴ ἀναρμόσατα εἰς τὸν σύνταξιν, πρὸς ἣν ὁ λόγος. ἀτύφως μὲν λαβεῖν, ἀλύτως δ' ἀφεῖναι. Εἴ ποτε εἴδες χεῖρα ἀποκεκομμένην, ἢ πόδα ἢ κεφαλὴν ἀποτετμημένην χωρὶς τοῦ ποτὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ λοιποῦ σώματος, τοιοῦτον ἑαυτὸν ποιεῖ, ὅσον ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ, ὁ μὴ θέλων τὸ συμβαῖνον καὶ ἀποχωρίζων ἑαυτὸν ἢ ὁ ἀκεινώντων ἢ πᾶσαν [?] ἀποτερίζεται τοῦ ποτὲ ἀπὸ τῆς κοινῆς φύσεως ἑνώσεως· ἐπέφυκας γὰρ μέρος. νῦν σκῦτον ἀποκόψας. ἀλλ' ὧδε κομμὸν ἐκεῖνο, ὅτι ἐξεστί [?] πάλιν ἑνῶσαι αὐτὸν [?], χωρισθέντι, ἀκολουθῇ [?] πάλιν ξωελθεῖν. ἀλλὰ σκέψαι τὴν χρηστότητα, ᾗ τετίμηκε τὸν ἄνθρωπον. καὶ γὰρ ἵνα τῷ ἀρχῇ, μὴ ἀποχωρίζῃ ἀπὸ τὸ ὅλον, ἐπ' αὐτῷ ἐποίησε· καὶ ἀποχωρίζει πάλιν ἐπανελθεῖν, καὶ συμφῦναι, καὶ τῶν τὸ μέρους τάξιν ἀποκλαβεῖν, ἐποίησεν. ὥσπερ τὰς ἄλλας διωγμὰς ἐκ τῆς λογικῶν ἡδονῆς, ὅσον ἢ τὴν λογικὴν φύσιν· ἵνα καὶ παντὸς τῶν ἀπ' αὐτῆς ἐλλιφάμεν. οὗ πρότερον [?] ἐκεῖνο ἦσαν τὸ συνισταμένον καὶ ἀντιπαθῶνον, ὑπο-πολιτεύειν, καὶ καὶ τὰ τὰ οσ' εἰς τὸν ἐμαφμέ-νου, καὶ μέρος ἑαυτοῦ ποιεῖ, ἵνα καὶ τὸ λογικὸν ζῶον διώκειν ἄν κώλυμα, ὕλῳ ἑαυτὸν ποιεῖν, καὶ χρῆσθαί αὐτῷ ἐφ' οἷον ἂν ἡ ὥρμησε.
units.tr: If you have ever seen a hand cut off, or a foot or head severed from the rest of the body, you will understand that whoever refuses what happens, and separates himself from others, makes himself such a thing, as far as he can: he cuts himself off from the union of common nature. For you were made a part. Now you have cut yourself off, but in this is the goodness of nature: it is in your power to be joined again, and it is granted to the separated part to return and to be united once more. Consider the kindness by which God has honoured man: he has put it in man's power not to be separated from the whole, and, if he is separated, to return and be joined, and take up again the place of a part. As for the other pleasures of the rational nature, which is itself the chief one, we must not be carried away by them. Let us rather cherish whatever is most peaceful and most sociable, and make ourselves a part of the whole, and whatever hinders our rational living, let us regard as nothing, and use ourselves for whatever purpose our reason has set before us.

units.la: Μὴ σε συγχέιτω ἡ τὸ ὅλου βίου φαντασία, μὴ συμποδιζυνόεη ἐπὶ πονα οἷα, καὶ ὅσα πιθανὸς ἀιηγεγενναῖς[?]: ἀλλὰ καθ' ἕκαστον τὴν προϊόντων, ἐπέρωτα σεαυτὸν, τί τὸ ὄργυ[?] τὸ ἀφόεκτον[?] αὐύποιτον[?]. ἀμῶν ἤδη γὰρ ὁμολογήσου. ἐπεί-πα ἀναμίμνησκε σεαυτόν, ὅτι ὅτε μέλλον, ὅτε δὲ πρώχησ βαρεῖ σε[?]; ἀλλὰ ἀεὶ τὸ πιόν. ὃ δὲ καταμεκρωΐται, ἐαν αὐτὸ μόνον τοιεισίης[?], καὶ ἀσυλέγχης τῷ διάνοιαν, εἰ πρὸς ὅσο φιλὸν αὐτέχειν μὴ διώκετε. Μὴ πνῦν πε-ραγά[?]. ἡ τοῦ τῆς κυρίου σωρῶ[?], παίθεια, ἡ Πέρ-γαμος[?]; τί δὲ τῆ Ἀδελιανοῦ, Χωρείας[?] ὁ Διό-τιμος; γέλοιον. τί δὲ, εἰ πρὸς ἀπέκα ἐνο ἔντο, ἐμέλλον αὐαπανέειν; τί δὲ, εἰ ἀπὸ ἀνόνυο, ἐμέλλον καθίσε-σθαι; τί δὲ, εἰ ἤδοντο, ἐμέλλον ὅτι ἀδύνατοι εἶν; οὐκ ἡ τούτους πεῖσον μὲν χρήσις, ὁ γέροντες γενέσθαι, οὕτως ἐμαρτο, εἶτα ἀποθανεῖν. τί ἔν ὕστερον ἐμέλλοις ἐκείνοι ποιεῖν, τοῦτ' ἐν ἀποθανόντῃ[?]; λέγων ταῦτο, καὶ λύθρον οὐ ἡμελήσω. εἰ δικαιοσύνῃ βλέπεν, βλέπε ἡρίσ-νων, φησὶ σοφωτάτοις. δικαιοσύνης καταξαι· σαπκικῷ ἀρετῷ, οὐχ ὁρῶ, εἰ τῇ τῆς λογικῆς ζῷ· καταισχύνη[?]. ἡδονῆς δ' ἐρᾷ, τῷ ἐγκρατείαν, ἐὰν ἀφέλης τὸ σὸν ὑπόλημμα τῷ τὴν λυ-πὴν σε δοκοῦντ', αὐτὸς οὐ ζῷ· ἀσφαλεσάτῳ ἴσηκας. τίς αὐτός; ὁ λόχῳ, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐμὴ λόγος.
units.tr: Let not the image of your whole life disturb you, nor weigh you down with the many troubles you may foresee. Instead, at each present moment, ask yourself: what is this that is so hard to bear? For you ought to be ashamed to admit it. Next, remind yourself that neither the future nor the past weighs upon you, but only the present, and this is made small if you limit it to itself and do not allow your mind to pursue what is beyond it. Do not be troubled by what is now occurring. What did the lady Pergamus or the physician Diotimus gain? Ridiculous! What would they have done had they been burdened by [illness]? What would they have done if they had been sick? What if they had been poor? Had they not been made old by life, or lived to be old, and then died? What would they have done in their last hour that they cannot do in death too? Saying the same thing, and grieving over it, I have neglected nothing. If you look to justice, look at it with the eyes of the wise. If you look to rational virtue, you cannot see what it is to live in it, and you will not be ashamed. If you love pleasure, of self-control, if you take away your opinion that you are being grieved, the loss is nothing; you are not alive, and so you cannot be harmed. Who is this? Reason itself, but not my reason.

units.la: [Note: the faint margin number on the left beside the sixteenth line appears to be "ιο," (10).] λόγῳ. Ἐγὼ. ἑκὼν ὁ μὲν λόγος αὐτὸς ἑαυτὸν μὴ λυπέτω. ἐὰν δέ τι ἄλλο ὡς κακῶς ἔχει, συλλαβέτω αὐτὸ ὥσπερ αὐτῆς. Ἐμπόδισμὸς αἰσθήσεως, κακὸν ζωϊκῆς φύσεως. ἐμπόδισμὸς ὁρμῆς, ὁμοίως κακὸν ζωτικῆς φύσεως. ἔστι δέ τι ἄλλο ὁμοίως ἐμποδιστικὸν, καὶ κακὸν τῆς φυτικῆς κατα-σκευῆς. ὥστε τοίνυν ἐμπόδισμὸς νοῦ, κακὸν νοερᾶς φύσεως. πάντα δὴ ταῦτα, ὡς σεαυτὸν μεταθέρε. τόνος, ἡδονή, ἀπλετά σε; ὅ[?] ἡ αἴσθησις· ὁρμὴ[?] σῶμα ἐγένετο; εἰ μὲν ἀνυποξαμερέτως ὥρμας ἤδη ὡς λογικῆς κακὸν. ἐὰν δὲ κοινὸν λαμβάνῃς, ὅπω βλάπτει, ἐὰν δὲ ἐμποδίζῃ. τὰ μὲν τοῦ νοῦ ἴδια, ὁ δὲ εἰς ἄλλου εἰωθεν ἐμποδίζειν. τοῦτο γὰρ, ὁ πῦρ, ὁ σίδηρος, ὁ τύραννος, ὁ βλασφημία, ὅχ ὅπερ ἀπλε[?]· ὅταν γὰρ ἡ σφαῖρα, κυκλοτερὴς μένει. Οὐκ ἐὰν μὴ ἄξιος ἐμαυτὸν λυπεῖν· ἐδὲ γε[?] ἄλλον πώποτε ἐκφὼν ἐλύπησα. δύφρανά[?] ἄλλον, ἄλλο· ἐμὲ δὲ ἐὰν ὑγιὲς ἔχω ἡγεμονικὸν, μὴ ἀχρηςεφόμενον, μήτε ἀνθρωπῶν τινα, μήτε τῶν ἀνθρώποις συμβαινόντων· ἀλλὰ τῶν ἀπὸ βλεπόντων ὀφθαλμοῖς ὁρῶντα, καὶ δεχόμενον, μὴ χρώμενον ἑκάστῳ κατ᾽ ἀξίαν. ὅστις ἡ ἰδὼ δὴ ὃν χρόνον σε ὠ τῷ χαλεπῷ. Οἱ τ᾽ ὕστεροφημίαν μᾶλλον διώκοντες, ὃ λογίζονται, ὅτι ἄλλοι τοιοῦτοι μέλλουσιν ἐκεῖνοι εἶν, οἷοί εἰσιν ἕτοι, ὃς βαρύνονται. κἀκεῖνοι δὲ θνητοὶ. Τί δὲ ὅλως πρὸς σὲ, αὖ ἐκεῖνοι φωνὰς τοιαύτας ἀπηχῶσιν, ἢ ὑπολήψμεν διαχύτω πρὸς σὲ ἔχωσιν. Ἄρον με, καὶ βάλλε ὅπου θέλεις. ἐκεῖ γὰρ ἔξω τὴν ἐμὴν ψυχὴν ἵλεων [?], τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἀκηκέμενον, ἐὰν ἐγὼ συγγρα[?]ῇ ζῶσι ἐν ἑαυτῇ κατασκευῇ. ἆρα οὖν ἄξιον; ἵνα οἱ αὐτοὶ κακῶς μὲ ἔχῃ ψυχὴ, καὶ χέρσον ἔχων τῆς ἡ, τὰ πφυσμένα, ὀργιζόμενον, ξωδυομένη, πηνρομένη; καὶ τί δύσκολος τότε ἄξιον; Ἀνθρώπῳ οὐδὲν ἐνὶ συμβαίνει τῶν ἰδίων, ὃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἀνθρωπικὸν σύμπτωμα· ἀλλὰ βοΐ, ὃ οὐκ ἔστι βοϊκόν· ἀλλὰ ἀμπέλῳ, ὃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἀμπελικόν· ἀλλὰ λίθῳ, ὃ οὐκ ἔστι λίθῳ ἴδιον. εἰ δὲ ἐκάστῳ συμβαίνει, ὃ καὶ ἔωσεν, ἢ πέφυκεν, τί αὖ δυσχεραίνοις; τὸ γὰρ ἀφόρη-τόν σοι ἔφερεν ἡ κοινὴ φύσις. εἰ μὲν δὲ τί τὴν ἐκ τῆς λυπῆς, οὐκ ἐκεῖνο [?] ἀλλὰ τὸ σὸν αὐτῷ κείμενον. ἤδη δὲ ἤδη ἐξαλείφεται ἐπὶ σοι ἔσῃ. εἰ δὲ λυπεῖ σέ τι τὴν σὴν ἐν τῇ σῇ ἀλήθειᾳ, τίς ὁ κεφαλὴν διορθώσει δὲ δόγμα; ὅμως δὲ ἐν λυπῇ, ὅτι οὐχὶ δὲ ἔτι αὐθεγείας ὑμῖς σοι φαινόμενον, τί οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἐνεργεῖς ἢ λυπῇ; ἀλλὰ ἰσχυρότερόν τι εἴσεται· μὴ ἂν λυπεῖν· ὁ γὰρ πάθος ἡ αἰτία τῷ μὴ ἐνεργεῖσθαι. ἀλλὰ οὐκ ἄξιος ζῶ, μὴ ἐνεργούμενον τούτου. ἅπαξ οὖν ἐκ τοῦ ζῇν βυμένης; ἢ ὁ ἐνεργῶν ἀφθνήσκει ἅμα ἴλεως τοῖς ἐνισαμένοις. Μέμνησο ὅτι ἀκαταμάλχητος γίνεται, τὸ ἡγεμονικόν, ὅταν εἰς ἑαυτὸ συγγρασυγγραφῇ, ἀχρεῖον αὐτῷ, μὴ τοιοῦντι ὁ μὴ λέ[?]γει, καὶ ἂν ἄλλος παραπέμπηται [?]. Τί δ᾽ ὅτι ὁ παλαιὸς καὶ μετὰ λόγου πολυτεκμηρίωσ[?], κρίνην πρὸς τὴν διὰ [?] ζῶν χειρὸ πόλις ὅσῃ ἢ ἐλθεῖν[?] α παθῶν διὰ ὁ α. οὐδεὶς γὰρ ὀχυρωτέρος ἔχει ἀνθρώπῳ, ἐφ᾽ ὃ καταφυγῇ, ἀνάλογον λοιπὸς ἂν εἴη. ὁ μὲν ὃν μὴ ἐωρακὼς ζῶν, ἅμα ἦς· ὁ δὲ ἐωρακὼς, καὶ μὴ καταφεύγων, ἀτυχής. Μηδὲν τολμῶν σαυτῷ λέγε· ὦ οὐ πεπονημένα φαντασίαι ἀναγγέλουσιν. Ἤγγελται, ὅτι ὁ δάνος σε κακῶς λέγει· Ἤγγελται ζῶν; ὅ δὲ, ὅτι βλάπτει, οὐκ ἤγγελται. Βλέπω ὅτι νοσεῖ τὸ παιδίον. Βλέπω. ὅτι δὲ κινδυνεύει, οὐ βλέπω. οὕτως ἂν μὲν ἐμὲ ἀπὸ αὐτῆς τῶν πλούτων φαντασίας, καὶ μηδὲν χεῖρες οὐδὲ ἀπέλθῃς ἐπιλέγε, καὶ οὐδέν σοι γίνεται. Μᾶλλον δὲ ἐπὶ ἐγκρῶς γνω-ρίζων ἕκαστα τῆς τῷ κόσμῳ συμβαινόντων, σὴν πηγὴν; ἄφες. Βλέπει ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ; ἐκκλίνου· ἀρκεῖ μὴ πεσσπείπης, τί δὲ καὶ ἐγένετο τῶν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ. Ἐπεὶ καταγελάσῃ τὸν ἄνθρωπον φυσιολόγον, ὡς ἂν καὶ τὸν τίκτοντα, καὶ σπυτίως γελασθείης, κα-ταγνώσκωμεν ὅπου ἂν ἐργασθείῳ ξέσματα καὶ πολιτεύματα, τὴν καταγινώσκοντες ἐρᾷς. ναί τοι ἐκεῖνοι γε, ἔχουσι τοῦ χύτα ῥήξεως· ἡ δὲ τὴν ὄψεως φύσις, ἐξῶ οὐδὲν ἔχει, ἀλλὰ τὸ θαυμαστὸν τῆς τέχνης ταύτης ἐστὶν, ὅπ τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ ὁμολογεῖσασι ἑαυτῷ, ὡς ἂν δ' ἀνδρὶ ἀφαιρεθέντι, καὶ γηράσκειν καὶ ἄχρηστον εἶν δοκῶν, εἰς ἑαυτὸν μεταβάλλει· καὶ ὅπ πάλιν ἄμα νεκρὰ, ἐκ τύτων αὐτὴν, ποιεῖ· ἵνα μὴ τις οὐσίας ἐξωθεν χρή-ζῃ, μήτε ὅσον ἐκβάλλῃ τὰ σαπρότερα, προσ-δέκηται. ἀρκεῖται ἂν καὶ χώρα τῇ ἑαυτῆς, καὶ ὕλῃ τῇ ἑαυτῆς, καὶ τέχνῃ τῇ ἰδίᾳ. Μήτε οἱ ταῖς πείξεσιν ἀδιαφόρως, μήτε οἱ τοῖς ὁμιλίαις φύ-ξειν· μήτε οἱ τοῖς φαντασίαις ἀλλάσσεσθαι· μήτε τῇ ψυχῇ καὶ Θάπαξ ξωιλλεσθαι, ἢ ἐνθορυ-βεῖσθαι, μήτε οἱ τῷ βίῳ ἀχολεῖσθαι· κτείνουσι, ὑρεκακομοῦσι, καὶ τάρας ἐλαχίνουσι· τί δὴ ταῦ-τα, πρὸς δὲ τὸ δικαιοσύνην μηδὲν θαρρεῖ, φρε-νήρη, σώφρονα, δίκαιον; οἷον εἰ τις πᾶσας τὴν ἀμύνει, καὶ ἀλυκεία, βλασφημοῦσι αὐτῷ; ἢ δὲ ὁ ταῦτα ὕμω ἀναβλύσαι. καὶ ἢν πιλῶ ἐμβαλλῃ, καὶ ἢν κ[?]πείαν, τὰ [illegible, ~6 letters] ἀφοσκλάσει αὐ-τὰ, καὶ ἐπικυφ[?], ὁ [illegible, ~4 letters]· ἢ [illegible, ~8 letters]. πῶς δὴ ἂν πηγλὼ ἀσάνοαν ἔξης, ὁ μὴ φρίαρ; φύς σεχυ-πάσης ὥρας εἰς ἐλβυδείαν, μεΤα τ' ὁμμῦνας, ὁ ἄλλος, ἢ ἀδημόνως. ὁ μὴ εἰδὼς ὅτι ἔστι κόσ-μος, οὐκ οἶδα ὅπου ἐστίν. ὁ δὲ μὴ εἰδὼς πρὸς τί φύσεως, οὐκ οἶδα ὅσις ἐστὶν, οὐδὲ τί ὅσι κό-σμος. ὁ δὲ ἀπ τοῦ ϱωλ ἀφλιπώς, οὐδὲ πρὸς ὅ, τι αὐτὸς τὶ ἔστι· τίς ἂν φαίνεται
units.tr: Reason, I. Let reason itself not grieve itself. But if anything else is ill, let it bear its own affliction. The hindrance to sensation is an evil of the living nature; the hindrance to impulse is likewise an evil of the living nature. Something else too hinders in the same way, and is an evil of the plant-like constitution. So a hindrance to the mind is an evil of the intellectual nature. Consider all these things, and transfer them to yourself. Does pain, or pleasure, or the fear of death, touch you? Does sensation touch you? Does impulse? If these things have befallen you, they are an evil for the rational nature only if you judge them as such. But if you take them as common to the animal, and as harmful or hindering, you will judge rightly. Those things belong to the mind alone, and what belongs to another is accustomed to hinder another. For fire, iron, a tyrant, or blasphemy, are not hindrances to the mind; as a sphere remains round, so the mind remains itself. Let me not grieve myself, unless I am worthy of it; nor have I ever grieved anyone else. Let another be grieved by his own. But for me, if I keep my ruling reason sound, and not turned against itself, neither any man nor anything that happens to men will harm me. Those who pursue reputation more than peace should consider that the others will be such as they are, and as wretched as those they now hate, and that they too are mortal. What is it to you if they utter such cries, or hold such opinions of you? Take me up and throw me where you will; there my soul will remain calm, and will keep its own nature, that is, if I can keep myself in a condition of being content with my own design. Is it worth it, then, that my soul should be in an evil state, and that I should be angry, frightened, grieved? Nothing happens to a man that is not proper to man; nothing happens to an ox that is not proper to an ox; nothing to a vine that is not proper to a vine; nothing to a stone that is not proper to a stone. If each thing befalls what is natural to it, why then should you be indignant? For common nature brings what is inevitable to you. If anything grieves you, it is not the thing itself but your judgement about it, and this you can wipe out at once. If something in your own reason grieves you, who is to set right the opinion that you hold? And if you grieve only because what seems to you good is not yet done, why not rather act than grieve? But something stronger is in the way: do not grieve, for the cause of the passion is the failure to act. Yet I am not worthy to live if I do not act in this. Once and for all, then, shall I depart from life? The one who acts does not die, but is gracious to those who grieve. Remember that the ruling reason becomes unassailable when it shuts itself up within itself, and is useless to the one who does not speak, even when others gather around. For no fortress is stronger for a man to flee to, and the one who has not seen it is never safe; but the one who has seen it and does not take refuge there is unfortunate. Say nothing to yourself that goes beyond what the appearances report. It has been reported that a certain man speaks ill of you: but that he harms you has not been reported. I see that the child is ill: I see that. But that he is in danger, I do not see. Thus, if you keep to the appearance itself and add nothing to it, nothing happens to you. Rather, knowing well each thing that happens in the world, leave it alone. Does someone seem to be walking on the road? Step aside. It is enough not to be harmed by the thing that happens in the world. For if you despise a man as a natural philosopher, as one who conceives and gives birth to ideas, you may be mocked as one who cannot see that the world is ordered. Those who are ashamed of their own kind... We should condemn whoever is occupied with reforming their souls and customs, as they are in error. Yes, these people have some desire to be torn apart; but nature of vision is in itself nothing, and the wonder of this art is that it transforms into itself what seems to a man deprived of life, grown old and useless; and again, it makes it alive from the dead. So that no one needs anything from outside, nor receives anything more than what it casts out as corrupt. Let the land be content with its own, the matter with its own, and the art with its own. Let no one be indifferent to what is to be endured, nor fleeing from companionship, nor changed by appearances, nor at all times troubled in the soul, nor bored with life. Those who kill, curse, or spread disquiet, what can they achieve for justice? Nothing, if they are prudent, sober and just. What if someone should cast in the path of others the things that are beyond our power? Then let them be cast out, and let them be... How then can he who does not know the world, know where he is? And he who does not know the nature of things, does not know who he is, nor what the world is. And he who has lost the goal of his life, does not know to what end he is living, nor what he himself is. Who then can praise one who flees the judgement of others, or fame? Nor can they know whose they are, who do not know the things of which they are made.

units.la: σοι ὁ τὸν τὴν προθέσιν ἔπαινον φύγων ἢ δόξ[?], ἢ οἱ οὐδ' ὅσων ἐστὶν, οὐτὲ οἱ πῆνες εἰσι γινώσκειν. Ἐπαινεῖ δὲ ἀγ[?] ἐλθ[?] ἐπὶ ἀνθρώπου, πῶς τὰ ὥρας ἐχει[?]; ἀρ' οὐκ ἂν ἀλλ[?] ἀνθρώπῳ, ὃς ἂν ἀρέσκῃ ἐχει[?]; ἀρέσκει ἑαυ-τῷ ὁ μὲ τὰ νοῦν, ἐφ' ἅπαν[?] ἐσ[?] εἶν, ὅτις πέφασι[?]; Μὴ κἂν μόνον σι μπνεῖν[?] ὡς πῶς τὸ ἀρχὴν ἀεί; ἀλλὰ ἤδη καὶ συμφρονεῖν ὡς τὸ πάντα νοερῷ. ὃ ᾧ ἥ[?]τον ἡ τῷ νοερᾷ δυνάμεις πᾶντι κι-χῦ[?]. ὅτι ἀφοίτησε, ἀκόσου δυνάμενος, ὅπερ ἢ ἀερώδης τῷ ἀναπνεῦσι δυνάμενος. Γενήσεις μὲν ἡ κακία, ἀδεὶ βλάπτεται, ἡ κόσμον ἢ ἡ ξ' μέρος, ἀδεὶ βλάπτεται τὸν ἔτερον· μόνῳ ἢ βλακεῖα, ὅτι τοῦτο, ᾧ ὡδὶ πέφασι[?] ἡ ἀπιμλάχεαι αὐτῆς, ὅταν πέφυτ' ὅτως ἀλήθη. Τῷ ἐμῷ προαιρετικῷ ἢ τ' ὁλήσιον προαιρετικὸν, ἐπὶ ὅτις ἀδιάφορόν ἐστιν, ὡς καὶ τὸ σύνδυμα[?] πον αὐτῆς, ἡ ἢ σαρκίδιον. ἡ ἡ, ἐὰν ὅπ μάλιστα ἀλλήλοις ἐν ἡμᾶς γεγόναμεν· ὅμως τὰ ἡ κ[?] μοινικὰ ἡμῶν, ἕκαστον τῆ ἰδίαν κυείαν ἔχει. ἐπεὶ τοι ἐμέλλεν ἡ τῷ ὁλήσιον κακία ἐμοὶ καὶ κύνι ἐν; ὅπερ ἂν ἢ ἐδὲξεί τῷ θεῷ, ἵνα μὴ ἐπ' ἄλλῳ ἢ ἐμὲ ἀτυχεῖν. Ὁ ἥλιος καὶ τᾶ πεχύασ δοκεῖ, καὶ ὡς ἡντη γε κέχυται, ἃ μὲν ἐκκέχυται. ἡ γὰρ χύσις αὕτη, τὰ σὸς ἔστι[?]. ἀκτῖνες γὰρ, αἱ αὐγαὶ αὐτῶ, ἀπ' τῆ ἐντείνε-σ[?] λέγονται. ὅσπερ ἔσ π ἔστιν ἀκτῖς, ἰδ' ἡς αὐ-, ἡ διά-
units.tr: You who shun the praise of the many, or fame, and who know neither those people nor what sort of people they are: do men praise the one who looks after the things of the world, or the one who is content with what he has? Does not the mind that is pleased with itself, which is set on a single purpose, have a claim to that pleasure? Do not be content merely to breathe with the air that surrounds you; be content to think with the universal mind, whose power is diffused through all things, as the air is diffused and drawn in by all who breathe. Wickedness of the reasoning faculty does no harm to the reasoning faculty, nor does it harm the world or any part of it. Only the dullness of reason, which it has in common with the body, can hurt it, when it is judged by true reason. My own purpose and the purpose of another, which is to be indifferent to what is not in our power, is like the flesh and the small body within us. Although we have been made for one another, each of our own faculties has its own proper function. Otherwise the wickedness of another's ruling part would harm me and bring misfortune upon me, which God has not willed, so that I should not suffer on account of another. The sun seems to be poured out, and indeed it is poured out everywhere, but the pouring out is its extension. For these are its rays, and they are called rays from their stretching out, as the ray is a line extended from the sun.

units.la: ἐὰ δέ πως συ[?]ῇ, εἰς οἰκείωσιν οἶκον τὸ ἀφ' ἥ-λιε φῶς ἐπιδυόμενον Στοικῶ. γίνεται γὰρ κατ' αὐτὸ[?]· καὶ ὥσπερ διαιρεῖται δὴ πρὸς τὸ σπερμα-τικὸν, ὅτι ἂν ἀπαντήσῃ, διέξεργον[?] ὃν ἐπέχει ἀ-ἐξ αὐτοῦ, τὰ δὲ ἔστιν[?] ἡ δὲ καταλήψεν[?], ἐὰν δὲ ἐπε-σει[?]. ὅμοιον τῶν ἐν τῷ λύπῃ, ἡ διάχυσιν τῆς διανοίας, εἰν χωμάζω[?] ἐκχυσιν[?]· ἀλλὰ πάσιν, ἡ πρὸς τὰ ἀπαντῶντα κωλύματα, μὴ βίαιον, μὴ δὲ ῥᾳγδαίᾳ τῷ ἐπιφέρειν ποιεῖσθαι[?]· μηδὲ μὲν κατα[?]πίπτειν, ἀλλ' ἀσιαζ[?], ἡ ὠθ[?] ... [illegible, ~12 letters] ... ὃ ἐχει[?] τὸ στε[?] ἡ[?] τῆς αὐγῆς[?], τὸ μὴ πρακτ[?]ικὸν αὐτῷ. Ὁ δὲ[?] ἐν θάνατον φοβούμενον, ἡ[?] τοι ἀναισθησίαν φοβεῖται, ἡ αἰσθησιν[?] ἐπ-ροσαν[?]. ἀλλ' ἐτι ἐκ τι αἴσθησιν, ἀδὲ κακὸς τὶν[?] αἰσθησιν[?], ἀ[?]τε ἀλλοιοτέραν αἴσθησιν κτήσῃ[?], ἀλ-λοῖον ζῷον ἔσῃ, καὶ τὸ ζῷ[?] ὁ πανύον[?]. Οἱ ἄνθρω-ποι γεγόνασιν ἀλλήλων ἕνεκεν. Διδάσκειν, ἢ φέρε· ἀλλὰ βέλθ[?], ἀλλὰ νῦς φέρεται, μένοντοι νῦς, καὶ ὅταν βλάπτηται, καὶ ὅταν τοῖς σπέρμασιν ἐμφίπτηται, φέρεται κατ' αὐτὸν ὀλὴν ἦν[?], καὶ ἀὐτὸ τὸ περιέχον[?] εἰστίναι εἰς τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν ἑκάστῳ[?]· πρέχει δὲ καὶ ἑτέρῳ τινί[?], ἐστίναι εἰς τὸ ἑαυτῷ ἡγεμονικόν.
units.tr: When the light of the sun falls upon a body, it is taken into that body's own nature, as the Stoics say. For it is made like it. As the Stoic ruling part is drawn towards the seminal reason, whatever it meets it takes up into itself, and this it holds without strain, not with violence, not by a sudden impact, nor by sinking down, but by an easy and gentle reaching out. Nothing that is not capable of action can hold anything else in that way. But the man who fears death fears either the loss of sensation or a different sensation. Yet if you have no sensation at all, you will not feel any harm, and if you acquire a different sensation, you will be a different living being, and so the living being will cease to be. Men exist for the sake of one another. Teach them, or bear with them. The mind is carried along by its own nature in all things, and when it is hurt and when it is assailed by the seeds of thought, it is carried back to its own whole nature, and it is in the ruling part of each man, which is the same for all; and it is directed also towards some other thing, so that the ruling part is one for each person.

units.la: ΜΑΡΚΟΥ ΑΝΤΩΝΙΝΟΥ αὐτοκράτορος, τῶν εἰς ἑαυτὸν βιβλίον θ'.
units.tr: Marcus Antoninus, Emperor, Book 9 of the Books to Himself.

units.la: ἀδικῶν, ἀσεβεῖ. τῆς γὰρ τῶν ὅλων φύσεως κατεσκευασμένης τὰ λογικὰ ζῷα ἕνεκεν ἀλλήλων, ὥστε ὠφελεῖν μὲν ἀλλήλους κατ' ἀξίαν, βλάπτειν δὲ μηδαμῶς, ὁ τὸ βούλημα ταύτης παραβαίνων, ἀσεβεῖ δηλονότι· εἰς τὸ πρεσβυτάτω τῶν θεῶν [?] ἡ γὰρ τῶν ὅλων φύσις, οὐσία ἐστὶ φύσις. τὸ δὲ λέγω ὄντα πρὸς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα πάντα τὰ οἰκεῖα ἔχει. ἔπι δὲ καὶ ἀληθὲς αὐτὴ ὀνομάζεται, καὶ τὴν ἀ-ληθῶν ἁπάντων πρόπη αἰτία ἐστίν. ὁ μὲν ἐν ἐ-κὼν ψυδόμενος ἀσεβεῖ, κακόσον ἐζαπατῆν ἀδικεῖ· ὁ δὲ ἄκων, καὶ κακόσον διαφωνεῖ τῇ τῶν ὅλων φύσει, καὶ καὶ κακόσον ἀκοσμεῖ, μαχόμενος τῇ τοῦ κόσμου φύσει. μάχεται γὰρ ὁ ὡδὶ πάνυ ἀπὸ τοῖς ἀληθέσι φερόμενος πρὸς ἑαυτόν. ἀφορμὰς γὰρ πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς φύσεως, ὧν ἀμελήσας οὐχ οἷός τε ὅτι ἐνυν διακρίνειν τὰ ψευδῆ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀληθῶν. ἐμὲ μὲν ὁ τὰς ἡδονὰς ὡς ἀγαθὰς διώκων, σὺ δὲ πόνους ὡς καὶ κακὰ φεύγων, ἀσεβεῖ. ἀνάγκη γὰρ τὸν ζῶντα μέμφεσθαι πολ-
units.tr: Whoever does wrong acts impiously. For since the nature of the universe has made rational creatures for one another's sake, so that they help one another according to their worth and never harm one another, whoever transgresses its will clearly acts impiously. The nature of the universe is the nature of being, and it has its own relation to all existing things. It is also called truth, and it is the cause of all true things. He who lies knowingly acts impiously, since he deceives; he who lies unknowingly acts unjustly, since he disagrees with the nature of the universe and throws the order of the cosmos into disorder, fighting against the nature of the world. For he fights against nature who is carried by his own choice toward what is false, having neglected the means that nature gave him to distinguish the false from the true. He who pursues pleasures as good, and you who flee pains as evil, act impiously. For a living man must necessarily find fault with

units.la: ὡς πολλάκις τῇ κοινῇ φύσει, ὡς τὴν ἀξίαν παποτεμοῦνη [?] τῆς φιλίας καὶ τοῖς οἰκείοις. Ἀλλὰ δὲ πολλάκις οὖν μὲν φίλους οὐ ἡδονῆς εἶναι, καὶ τὰ πολιτικὰ τούτων κτᾶσθαι· οὐ δὲ συνουσιαστικοὺς, πόφ, καὶ ὡς πολιτικῆς τύτε ὡ δεὶ πάντων. ἐπὶ δὲ ὁ φοβούμενος οὖν πονοῦς, φοβεῖ ἡ πατρὶ τὴν ἐσομέ-νην [?] τι τῷ κόμῳ. ἐἶς δὲ ἤδη ἀσεδεῖς. ὅτι διώκων τὰς ἡδονὰς, οὐκ ἀφίξεται τὴν ἀδικίαν. ἴσως δὲ ἀκραγῆς ἀσεβεῖς. χρὴ δὲ πῶς ἄ ἡ κοινὴ φύσις ἐπίσης ἔχει (ὁ γὰρ ἀμφότερα ἐποίει, εἰ μὴ πρὸς ἀμφότερα ἐπίσης ἔχει) πρὸς τοῦτο ὁ ὃ οὖν τὴν φύσει βουλομένους ἑπεσθαι, ὁμολογουμένως ὄντας ἐ-πίσης ἐξικεῖσθαι. ὅσις ἂν πρὸς τοὺς καὶ ἡδονὰς, ἢ θάνατον ἢ ζωὴν, ἢ δόξαν ἢ ἀδοξίαν, οἷς ἐπίσης ἢ τὴν ὅλην φύσις χρῆται, αὐτὸς οὐκ ἐπίσης ἔχει, δῆλον ὡς ἀσεβεῖ. λέγω δὲ τὸ χρῆσθαι τούτοις ἐπίσης τῷ κοινῷ φύσιν, αὐτὴ τῆς κατὰ δὲ συνεαύξη ἐπίσης κατὰ δὲ ἐξῆς γινο-μένοις, ὃ ἀδιγνομένοις ὁρμὴ πινὶ ἀρχαίᾳ τῆς προνοίας καὶ ἐπὶ ἰὼ ἀπὸ πινὸς ἀρχῆς ὥρμησεν ἐπὶ τῷ δὲ τῷ ἀκολουθήσῃ, συλλαβοῦσα πινὰς λόγους τῆν ἐσομένων, ὁ ἀδιαμάχως γονίμους ἀ-φοείσαι, ἀνασάσεων τε, ὁ μεταβολῆς ὁ ἀδοχῶς τοιοῦτον. Χαιτέρου μὲν ἰὼ ἀν-δρὸς ἄγλυτον ἐνλογίας, καὶ πάσης ὑπο-κείσεως κείσεως καὶ τρυφῆς καὶ τύφου γινόμενον, ὧν ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἀπωλέσθαι. τὸ δ' ἂν κορεσθῇ αὐτὰ γ' ἐκ τῆς [?] ἀκρασίας ἀπαλλάττεσθαι [?], ἀλλὰ πειθέσθω φύγειν ἐν τῷ λοιμῷ. λοιμὸς γὰρ ἢ διάνοιας φθορὰ ἐλάττων, μᾶλλον ἢ πνεῦμα ἢ τὰ περιέχοντα [?] τῇ κρασίᾳ καὶ τροπῇ. αὕτη μὲν γὰρ ζώων λοιμὸς καὶ ζῶα. εἰσὶν ἐκεῖναι δὲ ἀνθρώπων καὶ ἀνθρωποι εἰσιν. μὴ καταφρόνει θανάτου, ἀλλὰ εὐχαρίστει αὐτῷ, ὡς καὶ τοῦτο ἑνὸς ὄντος, ὧν ἡ φύσις ἐκλέλοιπεν. οἷον γὰρ δεῖ τὸ τέκνον, ἢ τὸ γηράσαι ἢ τὸ αὐξῆσαι, καὶ τὸ ἀκμάσαι, καὶ ὀδόντας, καὶ γένυν, ἢ πολιὰς ἐγγενεῖν, καὶ σωφρονεῖν, καὶ νυκτοφορήσαι, καὶ ἀφηνιάσαι, καὶ τὰ ἄλλα τὰ φυσικὰ ἐνεργήματα, ὅσα αἱ τοῦ βίου ὧραι φέρουσιν, τοιοῦτο τὸ θάνατος. ἡ μὲν οὖν κατὰ ἀνθρώπων ἐστὶ λελογισμένον, μὴ ὀλοθρεύεσθαι, μηδὲ ὠσπερ ὑπερηφανεύεσθαι πρὸς τὸν θάνατον ἔχειν· ἀλλὰ τῷ εἰμαρμένῳ ὡς μίαν τῆς φυσικῆς ἐνεργείας, ὡς νῦν τὸ εἰμαρμένης, τότε ἐμβρυον ἐν τῇ γαστρὸς τῆς γυναικὸς ὁμοίως ἐξέλθῃ, ἵνα ἐκδέχεσθαι τὴν ὥραν οὗ ἡ ψυχάριον οὗ τῆς ἐλύτρας τότε ἐκπέμπεται. ἐὰν δὲ ἴδιωτικὸν πραγμα ἀφιερωμένον ἡδέως, μᾶλλον δὲ σὺ κῶλον πρὸς τὸν θάνατον ποιήσει, ἢ ἐπίστασις ἢ ὡς τὰ ὑγρὰ κέμνα [?].
units.tr: ...often with the common nature, because he disregards the worth of friendship and of his own kin. Often, too, those who pursue pleasure become friends of pleasure rather than of human beings, and acquire the civic things for their own sake, not as companions in life. ... He who fears pains, fears for the body and for what will happen to it. And some are already impious because, in pursuing pleasures, they will not avoid injustice; perhaps they are wholly impious. For the common nature stands equally toward all things, since if it treated both the same way and yet not equally toward both, it would not... Those who wish to follow nature, agreeing to be equally disposed, are to be commended. Whoever does not stand equally toward pleasures or pains, life or death, glory or dishonour, which the whole nature uses equally, clearly acts impiously. I say that the common nature uses these things equally, as it brings about things in succession, from some ancient beginning of providence, from the first impulse, and so on through the ages, forming certain reasons for what is to come and preserving the power of change and transformation. ... The man who is unshaken in his rational judgement, and free from all pretence, luxury and vanity, is to be counted among the destroyed. But if they are satisfied with these things, let them not leave the plague of unrestraint, but let them be persuaded to flee from the plague. For corruption of the mind is a worse plague than the corruption of the air that surrounds us, by its mixture and change. The one is a plague of living things, the other of human beings. Do not despise death, but be thankful for it, since it too is one of the things nature wills. For just as it is natural for childhood, old age, growth, and the flower of youth, for teeth, beard, grey hair, begetting children, wisdom, ... and the other natural operations which the seasons of life bring, so is death. A reasonable person therefore should neither be destroyed by death nor hold himself proudly against it, but await it as one of the operations of nature, just as you now await the time when the embryo in the womb of a woman comes out, so that the soul may be released from its shell at its appointed hour. But if you are troubled by such a thing, you must consider how to make yourself steady toward death, ... and the things you are about to leave behind.

units.la: κἀάλια, ὧν μέλλης ἀφίσαθαι. Ὅμετ’ οἶων ἡδῶν[?] ἔσται ἡ ἐμπεφυρμένη[?]. πρόσκηπτεαζ μὲν γε[?] ὡς τοῖς ἡμῖν[?] σὺ ἔσται δεῖ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡδέως θαι, ὡς πρέπει φέρειν. μεμνῆσθαι μέντοι ὅτι ἐκ ἀπ' ἀνθρώπων ὁμολογματούντων σοι ἡ ἀπαλλαγὴ ἔσται. ἐκεῖνο δὲ μόνον ἐπὶ ἡδὲ ἀρα αὐθέλκευσαι μὴ κατάσχειν ἐν τῷ ζῷ, εἰ συζῷ ἐφέξειν τῆς τὰ ἰδιώτα δόγματα παθλωτος[?] οἷς. νῦν δ' ὁρᾶς ὅ-οσ' ὁ κοπτῶν ἐν τῇ Διαφωνίᾳ τ' συμβιώσεως, ὥστε ἐπ' ἂν, Θαῦμα ἐλλης ὦ Θάνατε μὴ πυ καὶ αὐτὸς ἀθλάσωμαι ἐμαυτῷ.
units.tr: ...You will be among those whose ways you are leaving behind. Do not be wretched, but gladly bear what must be borne. Remember, however, that the parting will not come from people who agree with you. This is the only thing that may draw us back and keep us in life: that we live together with those whose opinions are at odds with ours. Now you see how great a difference there is in living together. So if this happens, "Wonder, death, that I too might not..." and find my own peace with myself.

units.la: Ὁ ἁμαρτάνων ἐαυτῷ ἁμαρτάνει. ὁ ἀδικῶν ἑαυτὸν κακῶς, κακὸν ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν. ἀδικεῖ πολλάκις ὁ μὲν ποιῶν τι, ὁ μόνον ὁ ποιῶν τι. ἀρχὴ ἡ πῆσις ὑπόληψις κατα ληπτική, καὶ ἡ προῦσα πρᾶξις κοινωνική· καὶ ἡ παρὰ σα διάθεσις ἀναρεστική πρὸς ταν ἡ παρὰ τὴν ἐν τῆς αἰτίας συμβαίνον, Ἀχλεῖ φαντασίαν, σῆσαι, ὁρμῶ, σβέσαι ὄρεξιν, ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ ἔχειν τὸ ἡγεμονικόν, εἰς μὲν τὰ ἄλογα ζῷα, μία ψυχὴ διήρηται. εἰς δὲ τὰ λογικὰ μία νοερὰ ψυχὴ μεμέιεσαι. ὥσπερ καὶ μία γῆ ἐστὶν ἁπάντων τῶν γνωσῶν, καὶ ἓν φωτὶ ὁρῶ-μεν. Ὃ ἕνα ἀέρα ἀναπνέομεν, ὅσα ὁρατικὰ πάντα. Ὅσα κοινοῦ τινος μετέχει, πρὸς τὸ ὁμογενὲς ἀπολύδει. Τὸ γνωστὸν πᾶς-
